operations.description:
Retrieve a single task history entry by its unique identifier.

This operation returns a specific immutable audit record from the `erp_hrm_task_histories` table, which captures a single status transition event on a task. Each task history entry records the status immediately before the transition (`old_status`), the status immediately after (`new_status`), the exact timestamp of the change (`created_at`), and the organization member responsible for performing the change.

Task history entries are strictly system-generated and append-only. They are automatically created whenever a task's `status` field transitions from one value to another. Valid status values for both `old_status` and `new_status` are: `open`, `in_progress`, `completed`, and `closed`. These entries form a chronological audit trail that allows authorized viewers to reconstruct the full lifecycle of any given task.

Access to task history is subject to the same project membership rules as viewing the task itself. An authenticated member must be an active project member of the project to which the parent task belongs in order to view its history entries. Members who are not assigned to the project will receive a not-found or unauthorized response. Users holding the `project:manage` organization permission may view task histories across all projects in their organization regardless of direct project membership. Deactivated organization members are denied access consistent with their overall organizational access restrictions.

The path hierarchy — `/projects/{projectId}/tasks/{taskId}/histories/{historyId}` — ensures unambiguous identification: the `projectId` scopes the project, `taskId` identifies the specific task within that project, and `historyId` identifies the particular history entry. The system will verify that the task belongs to the specified project and that the history entry belongs to the specified task before returning data.

This endpoint is typically used alongside `PATCH /projects/{projectId}/tasks/{taskId}/histories` (the history list endpoint) for retrieving the full set of history entries, and `GET /projects/{projectId}/tasks/{taskId}` for viewing the task itself.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
1. Authenticate the requesting member and resolve their organization context.
2. Load the project record from `erp_hrm_projects` using `projectId`. Verify it exists, is not soft-deleted (`deleted_at IS NULL`), and belongs to the member's current organization.
3. Load the task record from `erp_hrm_tasks` using `taskId`. Verify it exists, is not soft-deleted (`deleted_at IS NULL`), and its `erp_hrm_project_id` matches the `projectId` from the path parameter.
4. Perform access control: check whether the requesting member has `project:manage` organization permission OR is an active project-lead for this project (via `erp_hrm_project_members`). If neither condition is met, verify the member has an active, non-soft-deleted record in `erp_hrm_project_members` for this project. If none of these conditions are satisfied, return 404 or 403.
5. Load the task history record from `erp_hrm_task_histories` using `historyId`. Verify it exists and its `erp_hrm_task_id` matches the `taskId` from the path parameter.
6. If any lookup fails the ownership/membership check, return a not-found response to avoid leaking existence information.
7. Join the organization member record (`erp_hrm_organization_members`) via `erp_hrm_organization_member_id` to include recorder details in the response.
8. Return the fully populated `IErpHrmTaskHistory` response object.

responseBody.description: The requested task history entry, including old status, new status, timestamp of the transition, and the recording organization member.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated and filtered list of timelog records within the authenticated member's organization.

Timelogs are the atomic work session records captured in the `erp_hrm_timelogs` table. Each timelog records a discrete block of work performed by an organization member on a specific date, tied to a project and optionally a task. The `duration_minutes` field stores the session length in whole minutes; the `billable` flag indicates whether the work counts against a project budget or client billing; and the optional `description` field provides free-text context about the work performed.

Access control follows permission boundaries: a standard member may only view their own timelogs. A member holding the `time:view_all` permission may view timelogs belonging to any organization member within the same organization, and may additionally filter by a specific organization member ID. Timelogs belonging to deactivated members remain visible to users with `time:view_all` to preserve historical accuracy for reporting.

The response is paginated and sorted by `work_date` descending by default. Filters accepted include: work date range (start date and end date), project ID, task ID, billable status (true/false), and — for privileged users — an organization member ID filter. All filters are optional and combinable.

Timelogs that have been included in a submitted or approved timesheet are protected records: they cannot be modified or deleted. Their `timesheet_id` field will be non-null, and clients should treat them as read-only. This context is useful when rendering a list view, as locked timelogs should be visually distinguished from editable ones.

This operation is typically used in conjunction with related endpoints such as `POST /timelogs` (create a new timelog), `PUT /timelogs/{timelogId}` (update a timelog), and `DELETE /timelogs/{timelogId}` (remove a timelog). Callers may also consult `PATCH /projects` and `PATCH /tasks` to obtain valid project and task IDs for filtering.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
1. Authenticate the requesting member and resolve their organization context from the session.
2. Determine access scope:
   - If the member does NOT have the 'time:view_all' permission, restrict the query to timelogs where organization_member_id = the authenticated member's own organization_member_id.
   - If the member HAS the 'time:view_all' permission, allow querying all timelogs within the organization. If a memberOrganizationMemberId filter is provided in the request body, additionally apply a WHERE organization_member_id = <provided value> filter.
3. Apply the following optional filters to the erp_hrm_timelogs query:
   - work_date >= request.startDate (if provided)
   - work_date <= request.endDate (if provided)
   - project_id = request.projectId (if provided)
   - task_id = request.taskId (if provided); validate that the task belongs to the specified project if both are given
   - billable = request.billable (if provided)
4. Validate that any provided projectId exists within the organization; return 404 if not found.
5. Validate that any provided taskId belongs to the project if both are specified; return 400 if not.
6. Execute the query with pagination: compute OFFSET from page number and page size. Default page size is 20. Sort by work_date DESC, then created_at DESC.
7. Join with erp_hrm_organization_members (for member display name), erp_hrm_projects (for project name), and erp_hrm_tasks (for task title, if task_id is non-null) to assemble summary records.
8. Include timesheet_id in the summary so clients can determine whether a timelog is locked (non-null timesheet_id that belongs to a submitted or approved timesheet).
9. Return a paginated envelope containing total count, current page, page size, and the data array of timelog summaries.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of timelog summary records matching the search criteria

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for filtering timelogs

operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information for a single timelog entry by its unique identifier.

Timelogs are the atomic records of completed work sessions within the ERP HRM system. Each timelog is owned by an organization member (erp_hrm_organization_members) and captures the work_date, duration_minutes, billable flag, optional description, associated project (erp_hrm_projects), and optionally an associated task (erp_hrm_tasks). They serve as the foundational data layer for timesheet aggregations, payroll-relevant records, and organizational reporting such as the Time Report, Project Budget Report, and Weekly Summary Report.

Access control is enforced at the service layer. An authenticated member (employee) may always view their own timelog records. A member who holds the 'time:view_all' permission within the organization may view any timelog belonging to any active or deactivated organization member in that organization. Requests for a timelog that belongs to a different member, without the appropriate permission, are rejected with an authorization error.

The timelog's relationship to a timesheet is reflected in the timesheet_id field. When a timelog has been included in a draft, submitted, or approved timesheet, this field references the corresponding erp_hrm_timesheets record. When a timelog's associated timesheet has been approved, the timelog is considered locked: it cannot be edited or deleted. The lock status should be communicated clearly in the response so that consumers know whether modification operations will be accepted.

The work_date field stores the calendar date on which the work session was performed. The duration_minutes field stores the work session length as a positive integer number of minutes, avoiding floating-point precision issues inherent in decimal hour representations. The billable field indicates whether the session counts against a project budget or is presented as client-billable in reports.

This endpoint is typically called after obtaining the timelog's ID from the timelog list operation (PATCH /timelogs), or after creating a new timelog. It may also be used to confirm timelog details before submitting a timesheet or before making an edit.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
1. Extract timelogId from the path parameter (UUID).
2. Look up the erp_hrm_timelogs record by primary key (id = timelogId). If not found, return 404.
3. Resolve the currently authenticated member's organization_member record for the current organization context.
4. Authorization check:
   a. If the timelog's organization_member_id matches the authenticated member's organization_member id, allow access.
   b. Otherwise, check if the authenticated member's role has the 'time:view_all' permission. If yes, allow access.
   c. If neither condition is met, return 403 Forbidden.
5. Additionally verify the timelog's project belongs to the same organization as the authenticated session to enforce data isolation.
6. Join related entities for the response:
   - erp_hrm_projects (project name, color, status)
   - erp_hrm_tasks (task title, status) if task_id is not null
   - erp_hrm_timesheets (status) if timesheet_id is not null — derive locked = (timesheet.status == 'approved')
   - erp_hrm_organization_members + member name via erp_hrm_members/UserProfile if needed for ownership display
7. Construct and return IErpHrmTimelog with all field values including the derived locked state.
8. Deactivated member's timelogs remain accessible to users with time:view_all permission.

responseBody.description: Detailed timelog record including work date, duration, billable flag, associated project, optional task, timesheet linkage, and lock status.

parameters.description: The unique identifier (UUID) of the target timelog record to retrieve.
parameters.name: timelogId

prerequisites.description: A timelog record identified by timelogId must exist before it can be retrieved. POST /erpHrm/member/timelogs creates the timelog entry that this GET operation looks up by primary key. Without a created timelog, the endpoint returns 404.

operations.description:
Create a new timelog entry recording a completed work session for the authenticated organization member.

This operation allows an employee to manually log a discrete block of work time they have performed. A timelog captures the essential details of a work session: the date on which work was performed (`work_date`), the duration of the session in whole minutes (`duration_minutes`), the project under which the work was done, and optionally the specific task the work relates to.

The `organization_member_id` of the newly created timelog is automatically derived from the authenticated member's session — the caller cannot log time on behalf of another member. The project specified must be one that the authenticated member is an active project member of; otherwise the operation is rejected.

If a `task_id` is provided, the referenced task must belong to the same project as the `project_id` provided. Mismatches between task and project are rejected.

The `billable` field indicates whether the recorded work session should be counted as billable time toward a client or project budget. If omitted, it defaults to `false`.

At creation time, the timelog is not yet associated with any timesheet (`timesheet_id` is null). Timelogs are later grouped into a weekly timesheet through the timesheet creation and submission workflow. Once a timelog is included in a submitted or approved timesheet, it becomes immutable.

This operation corresponds to the manual time entry path in the Weekly Time Tracking and Approval Journey. The alternative path — stopping a live timer — creates a timelog automatically via the Timer stop operation. Both paths produce records in the `erp_hrm_timelogs` table with identical structure.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
1. Authenticate the caller and resolve their active OrganizationMember record (erp_hrm_organization_members) for the current organization context.
2. Validate that the referenced project_id exists in erp_hrm_projects, belongs to the same organization, and is not deleted.
3. Validate that the authenticated member has an active project membership in erp_hrm_project_members for the given project.
4. If task_id is provided, validate that the task exists in erp_hrm_tasks, belongs to the same project (erp_hrm_tasks.erp_hrm_project_id == project_id), and is not deleted.
5. Validate that duration_minutes is a positive integer (>= 1).
6. Validate that work_date is a valid calendar date.
7. Insert a new row into erp_hrm_timelogs with:
   - id: new UUID
   - organization_member_id: resolved from session
   - project_id: from request body
   - task_id: from request body (nullable)
   - timesheet_id: null (not yet attached to any timesheet)
   - work_date: from request body
   - duration_minutes: from request body
   - billable: from request body (default false)
   - description: from request body (nullable)
   - created_at: current UTC timestamp
   - updated_at: current UTC timestamp
8. Return the full newly created timelog record as IErpHrmTimelog.
9. Edge cases:
   - Reject if project is archived, completed, or deleted.
   - Reject if member is deactivated.
   - Reject if task_id is provided but does not belong to the given project.

responseBody.description: The newly created timelog record with all persisted fields

requestBody.description: Details of the work session to be recorded as a new timelog entry

prerequisites.description: An active project must be created before a timelog can be logged against it. The timelog's required project_id must reference an existing, non-deleted project with 'active' status in the member's organization. Archived or completed projects reject new timelog creation.

The authenticated member must be assigned as an active project member of the target project before they can log time against it. Without an active project membership record in erp_hrm_project_members, the timelog creation request is rejected regardless of the project's existence.

operations.description:
Update an existing timelog record owned by the authenticated organization member.

This operation allows an organization member to modify a previously created timelog entry stored in the `erp_hrm_timelogs` table. A timelog represents a discrete completed work session capturing the date worked (`work_date`), duration in minutes (`duration_minutes`), the associated project (`project_id`), an optional task reference (`task_id`), billable status (`billable`), and a free-text description. All of these mutable fields may be revised through this endpoint.

Before applying any changes, the system enforces the approved-timesheet lock rule: if the timelog is currently linked to a timesheet (via `timesheet_id`) and that timesheet's `status` is `'approved'`, the update request is rejected entirely. The timelog remains locked for as long as its enclosing timesheet holds approved status. If the timesheet is subsequently rejected and reverts to draft, the lock is lifted and the member may edit the timelog again. This lock applies to all updatable fields without exception.

If the timelog is part of a timesheet with `'submitted'` status, editing is still permitted — only the `'approved'` status causes the lock. The system validates that the provided `project_id` references an active project within the member's organization; timelogs cannot be reassigned to archived or completed projects. When a `task_id` is provided, the referenced task must belong to the same project as the timelog.

The `duration_minutes` value must be a positive integer. The `work_date` must be a valid calendar date. Per the Timelog Ownership and Self-Logging Rule, only the organization member who originally created and owns the timelog (as identified by the `organization_member_id` column) may update it. Requests from any other member are rejected.

Related operations:
- `GET /timelogs/{timelogId}` should be called first to retrieve the current state of the timelog before performing an update.
- `PATCH /timelogs` lists timelogs with filtering and pagination for context.
- `GET /timesheets/{timesheetId}` can be used to inspect the timesheet status if the timelog belongs to one.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
1. Extract `timelogId` (UUID) from path parameter and look up the corresponding `erp_hrm_timelogs` record. Return 404 if not found.
2. Verify the requesting authenticated member owns this timelog (organization_member_id matches the current session member) OR holds an organization-level permission that allows editing others' timelogs. Return 403 if unauthorized.
3. If `timesheet_id` is not null on the timelog, query the linked `erp_hrm_timesheets` record. If its `status` is `'approved'`, reject the request with an appropriate error (timelog is locked due to approved timesheet) — do NOT proceed with the update.
4. Validate the request body fields:
   a. `work_date` must be a valid date.
   b. `duration_minutes` must be a positive integer (> 0).
   c. If `project_id` is provided, verify the project exists, belongs to the same organization, and has `status = 'active'`. Archived/completed projects cannot receive new time entries.
   d. If `task_id` is provided, verify the task exists and its `erp_hrm_project_id` matches the (updated or existing) `project_id` on the timelog.
5. Apply the validated changes to the `erp_hrm_timelogs` record and update `updated_at` to the current timestamp.
6. Return the fully updated timelog record as `IErpHrmTimelog`.
7. Error conditions: 404 (timelog not found), 403 (not owner or insufficient permission), 409 (approved timesheet lock), 422 (validation errors such as non-positive duration, inactive project, mismatched task-project).

responseBody.description: The fully updated timelog record reflecting all applied changes.

parameters.description: The unique identifier (UUID) of the timelog to update.
parameters.name: timelogId

requestBody.description: Updated field values for the timelog record, including work date, duration, project, task, billable status, and description.

prerequisites.description: An active project must exist before a timelog can be created or updated to reference it. The update body may reassign the timelog to a different project_id, which must also be an active project within the member's organization. If no active project exists, the timelog update referencing a project will be rejected with a 422 error.

The authenticated organization member must be an active project member of the project referenced in the timelog. Business rules require that only project members can log time against a project. Without an active project membership, both creating and updating timelogs for that project will be rejected.

The timelog record identified by `timelogId` in the path must already exist before it can be updated. The timelog is created via POST /erpHrm/member/timelogs, which produces the UUID used as the timelogId path parameter in this update operation.

operations.description:
Permanently removes a single timelog record from the system.

A timelog (stored in `erp_hrm_timelogs`) represents a discrete completed work session owned by an organization member, capturing the project, optional task, work date, duration in minutes, billable flag, and optional description. This operation permanently removes the specified record without any possibility of recovery.

Access is governed by two distinct permission tiers. The owning employee may delete their own timelog provided it is not currently included in a timesheet with `submitted` or `approved` status. If the timelog's `timesheet_id` is null or points to a timesheet in `draft` or `rejected` status, deletion is permitted. Attempting deletion while the timelog belongs to a `submitted` or `approved` timesheet will result in a rejection error.

Members holding the `time:manage` permission bypass the timesheet status restriction entirely and may delete any employee's timelog within the organization, including those associated with `approved` timesheets. This elevated authority is intended for administrative corrections and overrides the standard employee-level locking rules.

Because deletion of a locked timelog (associated with a submitted or approved timesheet) is blocked for regular employees, no real-time event is emitted for rejected deletion attempts. Events are only emitted when the deletion actually succeeds.

Upon successful deletion, the timelog record is permanently removed from `erp_hrm_timelogs`. If the timelog was linked to a timesheet, the timesheet's computed total hours will reflect the removal of this entry on the next calculation. Callers should verify the timelog's current timesheet association by retrieving its detail before attempting deletion if uncertain about eligibility.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
1. **Authorization**: Identify the requesting member's `organization_member_id` from the session. Fetch the timelog by `timelogId` (UUID). Verify the timelog exists; return 404 if not found.

2. **Ownership and permission check**:
   - If the requester is the owner (`organization_member_id` matches the timelog's `organization_member_id`): check the associated timesheet. If `timesheet_id` is not null, fetch the timesheet's `status`. If status is `submitted` or `approved`, reject with HTTP 422 (business rule violation: cannot delete a timelog included in a submitted or approved timesheet).
   - If the requester holds the `time:manage` permission: skip the timesheet status check and proceed.
   - Otherwise (requester is neither the owner nor has `time:manage`): return HTTP 403 Forbidden.

3. **Deletion**: Execute a hard delete (`DELETE FROM erp_hrm_timelogs WHERE id = :timelogId`) within a transaction.

4. **Activity log**: Record an activity log entry capturing the acting member, timestamp, and the details of the deleted timelog (project, duration, work date) for audit purposes.

5. **Response**: Return HTTP 204 No Content on success (no response body).

6. **Edge cases**:
   - If the timelog no longer exists at deletion time (race condition), treat as success (idempotent behavior or return 404 depending on policy).
   - Members with `time:manage` can delete timelogs belonging to any member in the same organization; validate organization scope to prevent cross-organization access.

parameters.description: The UUID of the timelog to be permanently deleted.
parameters.name: timelogId

prerequisites.description: A timelog record must be created before it can be deleted. The timelogId path parameter references an existing timelog in erp_hrm_timelogs; if no timelog exists with that UUID, the operation returns 404.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated and filtered list of timesheets within the organization.

This operation returns a bounded, paginated collection of timesheet records from the `erp_hrm_timesheets` table. A timesheet represents a formal weekly (Monday–Sunday) grouping of an employee's timelogs, submitted for managerial review and approval. Each timesheet is owned by exactly one `erp_hrm_organization_members` record and progresses through a status lifecycle: **draft** → **submitted** → **approved** or **rejected**.

Access to timesheets is strictly permission-gated. An authenticated member (employee) may only view timesheets that belong to themselves — i.e., records where `organization_member_id` matches the caller's own organization member ID. Attempting to list another employee's timesheets without elevated privileges is denied. Members who hold the **time approve** permission may view all timesheets across the organization, particularly those in the `submitted` state, to perform approval or rejection actions. Members who hold the **time view all** permission may view every timesheet regardless of status for any employee in the organization.

Results can be filtered by **status**, restricting the list to timesheets matching one or more of the four allowed statuses: `draft`, `submitted`, `approved`, or `rejected`. Results can also be filtered by a **date range**, limiting results to timesheets whose calendar week falls within the specified start and end boundaries (aligned to the `week_start_date` and `week_end_date` columns). Both filters may be combined simultaneously, in which case only timesheets satisfying all criteria are returned.

For timesheets that have been approved or rejected, the response summary includes the reviewer's identity (reviewer `erp_hrm_organization_members` reference) and the `reviewed_at` timestamp, giving employees and managers visibility into who acted and when. If a timesheet was rejected, the `rejection_reason` is also accessible.

The total hours for each timesheet are derived from the sum of durations of the associated `erp_hrm_timelogs` records; this is a computed value and is not stored directly on the timesheet row.

Pagination is cursor/page-based and returns a bounded set of results per page. The caller may control page size and sort order within the request body. This operation should typically be preceded by reviewing organization member context to understand which employee's timesheets are being browsed.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
1. Authenticate the caller and resolve their organization_member_id from the active session and current organization context.
2. Determine access scope:
   - If the caller has 'time_view_all' permission: query all timesheets within the organization (join erp_hrm_organization_members on organization_member_id to scope by organization_id).
   - Else if the caller has 'time_approve' permission: same broad access (can view all statuses org-wide).
   - Else: restrict query to timesheets where organization_member_id = caller's own organization_member_id.
3. Apply filters from the request body:
   - status filter: WHERE status IN (requested statuses), if provided.
   - date range filter: WHERE week_start_date >= rangeStart AND week_end_date <= rangeEnd, if provided.
4. Join with erp_hrm_organization_members (reviewer) to attach reviewer information (reviewer_id, reviewed_at, rejection_reason) for approved/rejected timesheets.
5. Compute total_hours per timesheet by summing duration from erp_hrm_timelogs WHERE timesheet_id = timesheet.id (either as a subquery or aggregated join).
6. Apply pagination: use page + limit or cursor-based pagination as specified in request body.
7. Apply sorting: default sort by week_start_date DESC (most recent week first), or as specified in request body.
8. Return paginated results as IPageIErpHrmTimesheet.ISummary with pagination metadata (total count, current page, page size).
9. Edge cases:
   - If the caller lacks permission and requests another member's timesheets, return 403.
   - If no timesheets match the criteria, return an empty page (not 404).
   - Deleted organization members (deleted_at IS NOT NULL) should still appear as historical owners but clearly marked.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of timesheet summaries matching the specified search criteria.

requestBody.description: Search criteria including status filter, date range filter, and pagination parameters for listing timesheets.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single timesheet record by its unique identifier.

This operation returns the full details of a timesheet belonging to an organization member, including its current status in the review lifecycle (draft, submitted, approved, or rejected), the calendar week it covers (week_start_date always being a Monday, week_end_date always being the following Sunday), and all associated timelog entries that contribute to the total hours calculation.

Access to a timesheet is governed by strict permission rules. An employee may only retrieve a timesheet they own (i.e., where their organization member ID matches the timesheet's organization_member_id). Attempting to access another employee's timesheet without sufficient privilege results in a permission denial. Users who hold the `time:approve` permission code within the organization may view all submitted timesheets to facilitate the approval and rejection workflow. Users who hold the `time:view_all` permission code may view all timesheets across the organization regardless of status. Any access attempt by a member who lacks both of these elevated permissions and is not the timesheet owner is rejected.

When the timesheet has been approved or rejected, the response includes the reviewer's organization member identity (reviewer_id) and the timestamp at which the review action was taken (reviewed_at), providing a clear audit trail. If the timesheet was rejected, the rejection_reason field will contain the mandatory textual explanation provided by the reviewer, enabling the employee to understand what corrections are required before resubmission.

The total hours figure is not stored as a direct column on the erp_hrm_timesheets table; it is computed from the sum of duration_minutes across all erp_hrm_timelogs records linked to this timesheet. The service layer must derive this calculated value and include it in the response.

Related operations: use PATCH /timesheets to list and search timesheets with filters. Use POST /timesheets to create a new draft timesheet. Use PUT /timesheets/{timesheetId} to submit, approve, or reject a timesheet.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
1. Extract the authenticated member's organization_member_id from the current session context.
2. Query erp_hrm_timesheets WHERE id = timesheetId. If no record is found, return 404.
3. Authorization check:
   a. If the requesting member's organization_member_id equals the timesheet's organization_member_id → allow.
   b. Else, look up the member's role permissions. If the role includes 'time_approve' OR 'time_view_all' permission codes → allow.
   c. Otherwise → return 403 Forbidden.
4. Also verify that the timesheet belongs to the same organization as the requesting member (organization scope isolation via erp_hrm_organization_members.organization_id).
5. Join erp_hrm_timelogs WHERE timesheet_id = timesheetId to retrieve all associated timelogs. Compute total_minutes = SUM(duration_minutes) over the linked timelogs.
6. If reviewer_id is not null, optionally join erp_hrm_organization_members for reviewer identity details to include in the response.
7. Construct and return the IErpHrmTimesheet response DTO including: id, organization_member_id, reviewer_id, status, week_start_date, week_end_date, submitted_at, reviewed_at, rejection_reason, total_minutes (computed), timelogs list, created_at, updated_at.

responseBody.description: Detailed timesheet record including owner, reviewer identity, status, week boundaries, associated timelogs, and audit timestamps.

parameters.description: The UUID of the target timesheet to retrieve.
parameters.name: timesheetId

prerequisites.description: A timesheet record must be created before it can be retrieved by its unique identifier. The timesheetId path parameter references the primary key of a record in erp_hrm_timesheets; without a prior POST to create that record, this GET will return 404.

operations.description:
Create a new timesheet for the authenticated organization member, covering a specific calendar week.

A timesheet is a formal weekly record that groups an employee's timelogs for a single calendar week (Monday through Sunday) and submits them for managerial review and approval. This operation creates a new timesheet in 'draft' status for the currently authenticated organization member. The timesheet's week is defined by its `weekStartDate` (always a Monday) and `weekEndDate` (always the following Sunday).

According to the erp_hrm_timesheets schema, no two timesheets for the same `organization_member_id` may share the same `week_start_date` (enforced by a unique composite index on `[organization_member_id, week_start_date]`). Attempting to create a timesheet for a week that already has an existing timesheet for the same member will result in an error.

Only active organization members may create timesheets. Deactivated members retain their historical records but cannot initiate new work entries, including new timesheets. The authenticated member's `organization_member_id` is automatically derived from the current session context and does not need to be supplied in the request body.

Upon successful creation, the timesheet is placed in 'draft' status and returned with all its fields, including null values for `reviewer_id`, `submitted_at`, `reviewed_at`, and `rejection_reason`, since these fields are only populated upon review actions. The employee may subsequently attach timelogs to this timesheet and then submit it for review via the separate timesheet submission endpoint.

Related operations:
- `PATCH /timesheets` — Browse and search existing timesheets with filter and pagination.
- `GET /timesheets/{timesheetId}` — Retrieve the detail of a specific timesheet by ID.
- `PUT /timesheets/{timesheetId}/submit` — Submit a draft timesheet for manager review.
- `PUT /timesheets/{timesheetId}/approve` — Approve a submitted timesheet (requires time approve permission).
- `PUT /timesheets/{timesheetId}/reject` — Reject a submitted timesheet with a written reason (requires time approve permission).
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Implementation steps:

1. Authenticate the requesting member and resolve their `organization_member_id` from the session context. Confirm the member's `status` is 'active' in erp_hrm_organization_members; if 'deactivated', return 403 Forbidden.

2. Validate the request body:
   - `weekStartDate` must be a Monday (ISO weekday === 1). If not, return 422 Unprocessable Entity.
   - `weekEndDate` must be exactly 6 days after `weekStartDate` (i.e., the Sunday of that same week). If not, return 422 Unprocessable Entity.
   - Both dates must be valid date values.

3. Check uniqueness constraint: query erp_hrm_timesheets WHERE `organization_member_id` = resolved member id AND `week_start_date` = provided weekStartDate. If a record already exists (regardless of status, except deleted/irrelevant states — the unique index applies unconditionally), return 409 Conflict indicating a timesheet already exists for that week.

4. Insert a new record into erp_hrm_timesheets:
   - `id`: generate a new UUID v4
   - `organization_member_id`: from session
   - `reviewer_id`: null
   - `status`: 'draft'
   - `week_start_date`: from request body
   - `week_end_date`: from request body
   - `submitted_at`: null
   - `reviewed_at`: null
   - `rejection_reason`: null
   - `created_at`: current timestamp (UTC)
   - `updated_at`: current timestamp (UTC)

5. Return the newly created timesheet record as IErpHrmTimesheet, including all fields populated as above, plus any joined reviewer/owner summary if the response DTO includes them.

responseBody.description: The newly created timesheet record in draft status with all fields populated.

requestBody.description: Information required to create a new draft timesheet for the authenticated member, specifying the calendar week to cover.

operations.description:
Update the status and review details of an existing timesheet record.

This operation advances a timesheet through its review lifecycle. A timesheet begins in the 'draft' state and can be progressed to 'submitted' by the owning employee, then to 'approved' or 'rejected' by a reviewer with the time approval permission. A rejected timesheet enters the 'rejected' state, which is editable — the employee may revise their timelogs and resubmit, transitioning the timesheet back to 'submitted' for another review cycle.

The `erp_hrm_timesheets` table records the full audit trail of each status transition. When an employee submits their timesheet, the `submitted_at` timestamp is recorded. When a reviewer approves or rejects the timesheet, the `reviewer_id` (referencing the reviewing `erp_hrm_organization_members` record), `reviewed_at` timestamp, and, for rejections, a mandatory `rejection_reason` are all persisted to the timesheet record.

Access control is strictly enforced: an employee (the timesheet owner) may only transition their own timesheet from 'draft' to 'submitted', or from 'rejected' to 'submitted' (resubmission). Users holding the time approval permission may transition a 'submitted' timesheet to 'approved' or 'rejected'. Any attempt to perform an unauthorized status transition, or to update a timesheet belonging to another member without the appropriate permission, is rejected.

Business rules enforced by this operation include: (1) A timelog included in an approved timesheet is locked — no edits or deletions are permitted while the timesheet remains approved. (2) Timesheets in 'submitted' status block organization deletion. (3) Rejection requires a non-empty `rejection_reason` explaining what the employee must correct before resubmitting.

Approving or rejecting a timesheet automatically generates a corresponding activity log entry ('Timesheet approved' or 'Timesheet rejected') within the organization's audit trail, including the reviewer identity and, for rejections, the rejection reason. These entries are visible to authorized members via the organization activity log.

Related operations: Use `PATCH /timesheets` to list and filter timesheets with pagination. Use `GET /timesheets/{timesheetId}` to retrieve a single timesheet's full detail including linked timelogs. Use `POST /timesheets` to create a new draft timesheet for the current week.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
1. Authenticate the calling member session and resolve the current organization context.
2. Fetch the erp_hrm_timesheets record by the provided timesheetId (UUID). Return 404 if not found.
3. Resolve the calling member's erp_hrm_organization_members record within the current organization.
4. Validate the requested status transition against the current timesheet status:
   - 'draft' → 'submitted': Allowed only for the timesheet owner (organization_member_id matches caller). Record submitted_at = now().
   - 'submitted' → 'approved': Allowed only for callers with the time approval permission. Record reviewer_id = caller's organization_member_id, reviewed_at = now().
   - 'submitted' → 'rejected': Same permission as approve. rejection_reason must be non-empty. Record reviewer_id, reviewed_at, rejection_reason, and reset status to 'draft' after rejection (or set status = 'rejected' per schema — the schema stores 'rejected' as a status and the employee can resubmit after edits).
   - Any other transition is invalid and should return 422 Unprocessable Entity.
5. Check authorization: if caller is not the owner and does not hold the time approval permission, return 403 Forbidden.
6. For 'submitted' → 'rejected', ensure rejection_reason is provided and non-empty; return 422 if missing.
7. Within a database transaction, update the erp_hrm_timesheets record: set status, submitted_at (if submitting), reviewer_id (if approving/rejecting), reviewed_at (if approving/rejecting), rejection_reason (if rejecting), and updated_at = now().
8. Return the fully updated erp_hrm_timesheets record as IErpHrmTimesheet, including related reviewer identity information.

responseBody.description: The fully updated timesheet record reflecting the new status, reviewer identity, and relevant timestamps.

parameters.description: The UUID of the target timesheet record to update.
parameters.name: timesheetId

requestBody.description: Status update payload for the timesheet, including intended status transition and optional rejection reason.

prerequisites.description: A timesheet record must be created before it can be updated. The PUT operation fetches the timesheet by timesheetId and returns 404 if the record does not exist. POST /erpHrm/member/timesheets creates a new draft timesheet for the authenticated member covering a specific calendar week, producing the timesheetId required by the path parameter of this operation.

operations.description:
Permanently removes a timesheet record from the system.

A timesheet is a weekly (Monday–Sunday) collection of timelogs owned by an organization member (`erp_hrm_timesheets.organization_member_id`), submitted for managerial review and approval. The status lifecycle of a timesheet progresses through: **draft** → **submitted** → **approved** or **rejected**. A rejected timesheet returns to draft status, allowing the employee to revise and resubmit.

This operation may only be performed on timesheets that are currently in **draft** status. Timesheets in `submitted` or `approved` status are considered active or locked and cannot be deleted. A rejected timesheet that has reverted to draft is eligible for deletion. If the requested timesheet is found in submitted or approved status, the system rejects the deletion request.

Only the owning organization member (`erp_hrm_timesheets.organization_member_id`) may delete their own timesheet. Members holding a role with the `time:manage` permission may delete any employee's timesheet within their organization, bypassing the standard ownership restriction, but the status constraint (draft only) still applies.

When the timesheet is deleted, all associated timelog records that reference this timesheet via `erp_hrm_timelogs.timesheet_id` are **permanently deleted** from the database as a consequence of the `onDelete: Cascade` constraint defined on the `erp_hrm_timelogs` foreign key. This is an irreversible side-effect: any timelog entries included in the deleted timesheet cannot be recovered after deletion.

This operation results in permanent data removal. The `erp_hrm_timesheets` record identified by `timesheetId` is irreversibly deleted from the database, and all associated timelogs are cascade-deleted along with it. No response body is returned upon success.

Prerequisite: The caller must be an authenticated member (`erp_hrm_organization_members`) within the same organization as the target timesheet. To retrieve the current status of a timesheet before attempting deletion, use `GET /erpHrm/member/timesheets/{timesheetId}`.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
1. Authenticate the requesting member and resolve their organization_member record.
2. Fetch the erp_hrm_timesheets row by the given timesheetId (UUID). Return 404 if not found.
3. Verify the timesheet belongs to the same organization as the requesting member. Return 403 if not.
4. Authorization check:
   a. If the requesting member is the timesheet owner (organization_member_id matches), allow proceed to status check.
   b. If the requesting member holds a role with 'time:manage' permission within the organization, also allow proceed to status check.
   c. Otherwise, return 403 Forbidden.
5. Status check: verify that the timesheet's status is 'draft'. If status is 'submitted' or 'approved', reject the request with a 409 Conflict or 422 Unprocessable Entity, indicating the timesheet cannot be deleted in its current state. A 'rejected' timesheet reverts to 'draft' per business rules, so it is eligible.
6. Perform the deletion:
   a. Delete the erp_hrm_timesheets record by id.
   b. Due to the Cascade relationship on erp_hrm_timelogs.timesheet_id, associated timelogs will have their timesheet_id cleared or be cascade-deleted per the configured database constraint. Verify and handle accordingly to avoid unintended data loss of timelog records.
7. Return HTTP 204 No Content on success.
8. Wrap the operation in a database transaction to ensure atomicity.

parameters.description: The unique identifier (UUID) of the timesheet to be deleted.
parameters.name: timesheetId

prerequisites.description: A timesheet record must exist before it can be deleted. This operation creates the timesheet identified by timesheetId. The timesheet must be in 'draft' status (which is the initial state upon creation) for deletion to succeed.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated and filtered list of active timer sessions within the current organization context.

This operation allows authenticated members to search and browse live real-time tracking sessions (timers) stored in the `erp_hrm_timers` table. Each timer record represents an active, in-flight time tracking session started by an organization member against a specific project and optionally a task. The `erp_hrm_timers` table enforces a unique constraint on `organization_member_id`, meaning at most one active timer exists per member at any given time.

Access control is applied based on the requesting member's permissions. A regular employee without the `time:view_all` permission will only see their own active timer (if one exists). A user holding the `time:view_all` permission — typically a Manager or Owner — can see all active timers belonging to any employee within the same organization, which is the primary data source for the organization dashboard's active timer display and workforce activity overview.

Search criteria include filtering by project, organization member, and whether a task is assigned. Sorting and pagination are supported to handle organizations with many concurrent active timers. The response includes timer details such as the associated project, optional task, optional description, and the exact timestamp when the timer was started (`started_at`), which clients use to compute live elapsed duration on the frontend.

This endpoint is typically pre-executed before starting a new timer (`POST /timers`) or when rendering the organization dashboard. The existence of an active timer for the current user can also be checked here before attempting to start a new one, as the system only allows one active timer per member.

Related operations:
- `POST /timers` — Start a new timer session (will fail if an active timer already exists for the member)
- `PUT /timers/{timerId}` — Update description, project, or task of a running timer
- `DELETE /timers/{timerId}` — Stop the timer and create a timelog, or discard without creating a timelog
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
1. Authenticate the requesting member and determine their organization context from the session.
2. Check if the member has the `time:view_all` permission (via their role's permission codes).
3. Build the base query on `erp_hrm_timers` joined with `erp_hrm_organization_members`, `erp_hrm_projects`, and optionally `erp_hrm_tasks`.
4. Authorization filter:
   - If the member does NOT have `time:view_all`: add a WHERE clause restricting to `organization_member_id = <current_member_id>`.
   - If the member HAS `time:view_all`: filter by `organization_id` only (all timers within the organization).
5. Apply optional search filters from the request body:
   - `projectId`: filter by `project_id`
   - `organizationMemberId`: filter by `organization_member_id` (only applies if requester has `time:view_all`)
   - `hasTask`: if true, filter WHERE `task_id IS NOT NULL`; if false, filter WHERE `task_id IS NULL`
6. Apply pagination: `limit` and `offset` (or cursor) from the request body.
7. Apply sorting: default sort by `started_at DESC` (most recently started timers first). Support sorting by `started_at`.
8. Return paginated results including timer id, started_at, description, project summary (id, name, color), task summary (id, title) if present, and organization member summary (id, name).
9. Compute total count for pagination metadata.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of active timer session summaries within the organization

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for filtering active timer sessions

operations.description:
Retrieve the details of a single active timer record by its unique identifier.

A timer (stored in `erp_hrm_timers`) represents a live real-time tracking session started by an organization member against a specific project and optionally a task. Because the system enforces at most one active timer per member at any time (via a unique constraint on `organization_member_id`), this endpoint is typically used to inspect the current running session of a known timer ID.

The response includes all fields of the timer: the owning organization member, the associated project, the optional task focus, the optional free-text description of the work being performed, and the `started_at` timestamp from which elapsed duration can be computed client-side. There are no `updated_at` or `deleted_at` columns on timer records — timers are transient and are permanently removed from the database when stopped (which creates a corresponding Timelog) or discarded (which removes the timer with no Timelog generated).

Access to this endpoint is governed by organizational membership and permissions. A member may retrieve their own active timer unconditionally. A member who holds the `time:view_all` permission within their current organization context may retrieve the active timer of any employee in the same organization. Attempts to fetch a timer belonging to a different member without the appropriate permission will result in a permission error.

To list or view completed time records, use the Timelog endpoints instead. To start a new timer, use `POST /timers`. To stop the running timer (creating a Timelog), use the timer stop endpoint. To discard the running timer without producing a Timelog, use the timer discard endpoint.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
1. Authenticate the requesting member and resolve their current organization context.
2. Look up the erp_hrm_timers record by the provided timerId UUID. If no record is found, return 404.
3. Verify authorization:
   a. If the timer's organization_member_id matches the authenticated member's organization member ID for the current organization, allow access.
   b. Otherwise, check if the authenticated member has the 'time:view_all' permission within the current organization. If they do, allow access only if the timer's owning organization member belongs to the same organization. If they do not, return 403.
4. Join the timer with erp_hrm_projects (on project_id) and optionally erp_hrm_tasks (on task_id) and erp_hrm_organization_members (on organization_member_id) to enrich the response with related entity details.
5. Return the fully hydrated timer record as IErpHrmTimer.

Edge cases:
- Timer not found: return 404 with a descriptive error.
- Member is not in any organization or not active: return 403.
- Timer belongs to a member in a different organization: return 403 even if the requester has time:view_all (cross-organization isolation).

responseBody.description: The full details of the requested active timer, including its owning member, associated project and optional task, optional description, and the timestamp when the session started.

parameters.description: The UUID of the target active timer record to retrieve.
parameters.name: timerId

prerequisites.description: A timer record must be created before it can be retrieved by ID. POST /erpHrm/member/timers starts a new active tracking session for the authenticated member, producing the timerId that is required as a path parameter for this GET operation. Without a prior timer creation, the endpoint will return 404.

operations.description:
Retrieve the authenticated member's currently active timer session.

This operation returns the live, in-progress timer that the calling organization member has started. Because the system enforces the business rule that each employee may have at most one active timer at any given time — guaranteed by the unique constraint on `organization_member_id` in the `erp_hrm_timers` table — this endpoint always refers to a single, unambiguous timer session.

The returned timer record includes the associated project (required) and optional task being tracked, the exact timestamp when the timer was started (`started_at`), an optional free-text description entered by the member describing what they are working on, and the timer's unique identifier. Clients are expected to compute the elapsed duration client-side using the `started_at` timestamp and the current wall-clock time, as the timer continues running indefinitely without any server-enforced timeout.

If no timer is currently active for the member — meaning they have not started one, or they have previously stopped or discarded it — the response body will be `null`, indicating no running timer exists. The client should use this to display the appropriate 'no active timer' state on the personal dashboard.

Access is strictly limited to the authenticated member's own timer. An employee cannot view another employee's timer through this endpoint. Users with the `time:view_all` permission who need visibility into other employees' timer states should use the organization-level timer monitoring endpoints. This aligns with the real-time dashboard synchronization behavior described in the Timer Events specification, where timer-started, timer-stopped, timer-discarded, and timer-updated events are delivered only to the owning employee's connected sessions through this personal scope.

The timer is a transient record in `erp_hrm_timers` and does not undergo any form of persistent deletion marking; it is permanently removed when stopped (creating a Timelog) or discarded (no Timelog created). Consequently, a successful response from this endpoint always reflects the true real-time state of the member's tracking session.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
1. Extract the authenticated member's identity from the session token to resolve their `erp_hrm_organization_members.id` (organization_member_id) within the current organization context.
2. Query the `erp_hrm_timers` table with a WHERE clause on `organization_member_id = <resolved_member_id>`. Because of the unique constraint `@@unique([organization_member_id])`, at most one row will match.
3. If no row is found, return a null response body (HTTP 200 with null or an empty/no-content indicator per the agreed API contract).
4. If a row is found, join with `erp_hrm_projects` to populate the project details (name, color, id) and optionally with `erp_hrm_tasks` if `task_id` is non-null to populate task details (title, id, status).
5. Return the assembled `IErpHrmTimer` object including: id, organization_member_id, project (id, name, color), task (id, title — nullable), description (nullable), started_at, created_at.
6. Do NOT compute elapsed seconds server-side; the client handles live elapsed time using started_at.
7. Authorization: verify the calling member belongs to the same organization and is accessing only their own timer. No cross-member access is allowed at this endpoint.
8. Edge cases: if the organization member is deactivated, the timer record should still be returned if one exists (deactivation does not automatically stop timers; however, deactivated members cannot start new timers — guard this at the start endpoint).

responseBody.description: The authenticated member's currently active timer session, or null if no timer is running.

operations.description:
Start a new real-time tracking timer session for the currently authenticated organization member.

This operation creates a new active timer record in the `erp_hrm_timers` table, representing a live work session the member is beginning. A timer is bound to exactly one project and optionally one task within that project. The `started_at` timestamp is recorded at the moment the timer is created, and it will be used to compute the elapsed duration when the timer is eventually stopped and converted into a timelog entry.

A fundamental constraint enforced by the system is that each organization member may have at most one active timer at any time. The `erp_hrm_timers` table enforces this through a unique constraint on `organization_member_id`. If the authenticated member already has a running timer, this request will be rejected. The member must stop or discard their existing timer before starting a new one.

The target project must be one that the authenticated member is currently assigned to as a project member. Providing a project the member is not a member of will result in a rejection. If a task is specified, it must belong to the selected project; tasks from other projects are not permitted. Providing a task that is not part of the given project will also result in a rejection.

The optional `description` field allows the member to note what they are currently working on during the session. This can also be updated later while the timer is running via the timer update endpoint without interrupting the session.

Once started, the timer runs indefinitely. There is no automatic timeout or system-enforced duration limit. The timer continues until the member explicitly stops it (which creates a timelog) or discards it (which removes the timer without creating any timelog).

This operation is only available to authenticated members and applies exclusively to the caller's own timer. A member cannot start a timer on behalf of another member.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
1. Authenticate the request and resolve the caller's organization member record from the session (organization_member_id).
2. Check whether the member already has an active timer by querying erp_hrm_timers WHERE organization_member_id = <caller_id>. If a record exists, return HTTP 409 Conflict — a member may have at most one active timer.
3. Validate that the provided project_id references an existing, non-deleted project within the same organization as the member (erp_hrm_projects WHERE id = project_id AND organization_id = member.organization_id AND deleted_at IS NULL). Return HTTP 404 if not found.
4. Validate that the member is an active project member of the given project by querying erp_hrm_project_members WHERE project_id = <project_id> AND organization_member_id = <caller_id>. Return HTTP 403 if not found.
5. If task_id is provided, validate that the task exists in erp_hrm_tasks WHERE id = task_id AND erp_hrm_project_id = project_id AND deleted_at IS NULL. Return HTTP 422 if the task does not belong to the project.
6. Insert a new record into erp_hrm_timers: { id: uuid, organization_member_id, project_id, task_id (nullable), description (nullable), started_at: now(), created_at: now() }.
7. Return the newly created timer record as IErpHrmTimer.

responseBody.description: The newly created active timer record for the authenticated member.

requestBody.description: Timer creation input specifying the project, optional task, and optional description for the new tracking session.

prerequisites.description: A project must exist before a timer can be started against it. The timer's required project_id field must reference a valid, non-deleted project within the authenticated member's organization. Without a prior project creation, the service returns HTTP 404.

The authenticated member must be an active project member of the target project before starting a timer against it. The service validates membership via erp_hrm_project_members and returns HTTP 403 if the member is not assigned to the project. The project membership record must be created before the timer can be started.

operations.description:
Update the editable fields of an active running timer.

This operation allows the authenticated organization member to modify their currently active timer while it continues to run uninterrupted. The timer being updated is identified by its unique UUID (`timerId`) and must belong to the currently authenticated member — an employee can only edit their own active timer.

The following fields may be updated: the free-text `description` describing the work being performed, the `project` against which the session is being tracked, and the optional `task` within the selected project. All edits take effect immediately without resetting, pausing, or interrupting the timer's elapsed duration.

If the `project_id` is changed to a different project, any previously associated task is automatically cleared, because the prior task no longer belongs to the newly selected project. The caller may then optionally provide a new `task_id` that belongs to the newly selected project. If a `task_id` is submitted without a project change (or alongside a project change), the task must belong to the currently effective project; otherwise the request is rejected.

The replacement project must be one that the authenticated employee is currently assigned to as a project member. Submitting a project to which the employee is not assigned will result in a validation error.

This operation is strictly scoped to the timer's owner. Users who hold the `time:manage` permission are permitted to edit or delete already-created timelogs, but they are NOT permitted to operate another employee's active running timer through this endpoint. Only the employee who started the timer may call this operation.

Related operations:
- `POST /timers` should be called first to start a timer session before editing it.
- `DELETE /timers/{timerId}` can be used to discard the timer without creating a timelog.
- `POST /timers/{timerId}/stop` can be used to stop the timer and convert it to a timelog.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
1. Authenticate the requesting member from the session context.
2. Load the timer record from `erp_hrm_timers` by the given `timerId` UUID.
3. Verify the timer exists; if not, return 404.
4. Verify that `organization_member_id` on the timer matches the authenticated member's organization member ID. If it does not match, return 403 — employees may only edit their own timer.
5. Validate the incoming request body:
   a. If `project_id` is provided and differs from the current `project_id`:
      - Verify the authenticated member has a `erp_hrm_project_members` record linking them to the new project. If not, return 403/422.
      - Clear any currently set `task_id` (set to null) unless a new `task_id` is also provided in the same request.
   b. If `task_id` is provided:
      - Determine the effective project: use the new `project_id` if it was changed in this request, otherwise use the current `project_id`.
      - Verify the task exists in `erp_hrm_tasks` and its `project_id` matches the effective project. If not, return 422.
   c. `description` may be any string or null; no additional validation beyond length limits.
6. Apply updates: UPDATE `erp_hrm_timers` SET project_id = ..., task_id = ..., description = ... WHERE id = timerId.
7. Return the updated timer record with all fields including related project and task details.
8. Note: No `updated_at` column exists on `erp_hrm_timers` per the schema — do not attempt to update such a field.

responseBody.description: The updated active timer record reflecting the applied changes.

parameters.description: The UUID of the active timer to update. Must belong to the currently authenticated organization member.
parameters.name: timerId

requestBody.description: Fields to update on the running timer: description, associated project, and/or associated task.

prerequisites.description: An active timer session must be started before it can be updated. POST /erpHrm/member/timers creates the erp_hrm_timers record identified by timerId. Without a running timer record, the PUT operation cannot find the target resource and will return 404.

operations.description:
Permanently discard an employee's active timer session without creating a timelog record.

This operation terminates and permanently removes the specified timer from the system. Unlike stopping a timer — which converts the elapsed session into a persisted timelog entry — discarding a timer destroys the tracking session entirely. No work record is created, and the elapsed time is lost.

The discard action is fully irreversible. Once a timer is discarded, neither the timer record nor the elapsed duration can be recovered by any means. The system provides no undo or recovery mechanism after the confirmation of a discard.

Access control follows a two-tier model. The timer's owner (the organization member whose `organization_member_id` matches the timer record) may always discard their own active timer. Additionally, users holding the time management permission (`time:manage`) within the organization are permitted to discard any employee's active timer — including timers not belonging to themselves. Employees who do not own the timer and do not hold the time management permission will receive a 403 Forbidden response.

The underlying `erp_hrm_timers` table stores transient timer records with no `deleted_at` column, confirming that timer records are physically deleted (not logically marked) when this operation is executed. The record is identified by its UUID primary key (`timerId` path parameter).

If no active timer with the provided `timerId` exists, the operation returns a 404 Not Found response. If the caller neither owns the referenced timer nor holds the time management permission, a 403 Forbidden response is returned. No partial state is left behind in any failure scenario.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
1. Authenticate the current member session and resolve their organization context.
2. Look up the erp_hrm_timers record by the provided timerId (UUID primary key).
3. Verify the record exists; if not, return 404.
4. Verify that erp_hrm_timers.organization_member_id matches the authenticated member's organization_member id for this organization context; if not, return 403 (even if the caller has time:manage permission).
5. Permanently delete the erp_hrm_timers record using a hard DELETE SQL statement (no soft-delete column exists on this table).
6. Return HTTP 204 No Content on success.
7. No timelog record is created at any point during this operation.
8. Wrap the delete in a transaction to ensure atomicity; any failure rolls back and the timer record is preserved intact.

parameters.description: The UUID of the active timer to be discarded.
parameters.name: timerId

prerequisites.description: An active timer session must be created before it can be discarded. The POST /erpHrm/member/timers operation starts a new real-time tracking timer and returns the timerId required by this delete operation. Without a pre-existing timer record, the discard request would return 404 Not Found.

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of organizational activity log entries.

Activity logs are immutable audit trail records that the system automatically generates whenever significant business events occur within an organization. This operation allows authorized organization members to browse, search, and filter through the complete chronological history of actions performed in their organization.

Each activity log entry in the erp_hrm_activity_logs table captures: the exact timestamp of the action, the organization member who performed it, a categorized action_type drawn from a fixed set of recognized business event codes (such as 'employee_invited', 'employee_deactivated', 'contract_created', 'project_archived', 'task_status_changed', 'timesheet_submitted', 'timesheet_approved', 'timesheet_rejected', 'role_assigned_or_changed', and others), the type and ID of the target entity affected, and optional supplementary details.

The organization scope is automatically determined from the authenticated member's current session context. All returned entries belong exclusively to the member's current organization, enforcing strict data isolation between organizations. Members must hold appropriate audit log viewing permissions within their organization role to access this endpoint.

This operation supports a rich set of filtering capabilities including filtering by one or more action_type values, by target_entity_type (e.g., 'member', 'contract', 'project', 'task', 'timesheet', 'role'), by the specific target_entity_id, by the performing organization_member_id, and by a created_at date/time range. Pagination and sorting are also supported, with results typically ordered by created_at descending so the most recent events appear first.

Activity log entries are permanently preserved for the lifetime of the organization and are never purged or overwritten. They cannot be created, modified, or deleted through any user-facing operation — this endpoint provides read access only. Refer to the ActivityLog business rules for the complete list of loggable action types and the entities they target.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
1. Authenticate the requesting member and resolve their current organization_id from the session context.
2. Verify that the member's role grants permission to view the organization's activity log (audit log viewing permission).
3. Accept IErpHrmActivityLog.IRequest in the request body, which includes optional filters:
   - action_type: string[] (filter by one or more action type codes)
   - target_entity_type: string[] (filter by entity type, e.g., 'member', 'contract', 'project', 'task', 'timesheet', 'role')
   - target_entity_id: string (UUID, filter by specific target entity)
   - organization_member_id: string (UUID, filter by performer)
   - created_at_from: DateTime (inclusive lower bound)
   - created_at_to: DateTime (inclusive upper bound)
   - pagination: { page, limit } for offset-based pagination
   - sort: { field, direction } for sorting (default: created_at DESC)
4. Build a query against erp_hrm_activity_logs filtered by organization_id from session (mandatory), plus any provided optional filters. Use the @@index([organization_id, created_at]) and @@index([organization_id, action_type]) indexes for efficiency.
5. Join erp_hrm_organization_members to resolve the performer's display name/ID for the summary response.
6. Return total count and the page of entries as IPageIErpHrmActivityLog.ISummary.
7. Each summary item includes: id, action_type, target_entity_type, target_entity_id, organization_member_id (and brief performer info), details (nullable), created_at.
8. Edge cases: if no entries match the filter, return empty data array with correct pagination metadata. If a filter references a non-existent member_id or entity_id, return empty results (not an error).

responseBody.description: Paginated list of activity log entry summaries matching the provided search criteria

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for filtering activity log entries

operations.description:
Retrieve a single activity log entry by its unique identifier.

This operation returns the full detail of one immutable organizational audit trail entry from the `erp_hrm_activity_logs` table. Each activity log entry is created automatically by the system whenever a qualifying business event occurs within an organization, and once recorded the entry can never be edited or deleted. The entry includes the exact timestamp the action occurred, the organization member who performed it, the categorized action type (one of a fixed set such as `employee_invited`, `employee_deactivated`, `employee_reactivated`, `contract_created`, `contract_edited`, `project_created`, `project_archived`, `project_completed`, `project_deleted`, `task_status_changed`, `timesheet_submitted`, `timesheet_approved`, `timesheet_rejected`, `role_assigned_or_changed`), the type and UUID of the affected entity (`target_entity_type` and `target_entity_id`), and any optional supplementary `details` context.

Access to this endpoint is restricted to authenticated members who hold the organization management permission (`org:manage`) within the organization that owns the requested log entry. The activity log is strictly scoped to a single organization; a member from a different organization cannot view entries belonging to another organization.

This endpoint is complementary to the paginated activity log list operation (`PATCH /activityLogs`), which supports filtering by action type, performer, and date range. Use this endpoint to retrieve the full detail of a specific entry identified from the list — for example, to inspect the `details` field of a particular contract edit or role assignment event.

Because activity log entries are permanently immutable (`erp_hrm_activity_logs` has no `updated_at` or `deleted_at` columns), the response for a given `activityLogId` will always be identical across repeated calls as long as the record exists.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
1. Authenticate the requesting member and resolve the current organization context from the session.
2. Verify the member has the `org:manage` permission within the current organization.
3. Query `erp_hrm_activity_logs` by the given `activityLogId` (UUID primary key).
4. Verify the retrieved entry's `organization_id` matches the authenticated member's current organization. If not, return 403 Forbidden (cross-organization access denial).
5. If no entry is found for the given UUID, return 404 Not Found.
6. Join or hydrate the `organization_member_id` to include identifying details of the performer (e.g., name, email) for the response DTO.
7. Return the full activity log entry as `IErpHrmActivityLog`, including: id, organization_id, organization_member_id (with performer summary), action_type, target_entity_type, target_entity_id, details (nullable), and created_at.
8. No write operations are performed; this is a pure read-only query.

responseBody.description: The full detail of the requested activity log entry.

parameters.description: The UUID of the target activity log entry to retrieve.
parameters.name: activityLogId

operations.description:
Transfer ownership of an organization from the current owner to another active organization member.

This operation allows the organization's current Owner to hand over their ownership role to an existing active member of the same organization. The designated recipient must already be a member of the organization with an active status. Upon completion, the recipient is elevated to the Owner role, and the outgoing owner is reassigned to a non-Owner role as specified in the request body. The organization will always have exactly one owner at any point in time.

Only the current Owner of the organization may invoke this endpoint. Members holding any other role — including Manager — are not authorized to perform an ownership transfer. Any unauthorized attempt will be rejected.

Ownership transfer is a critical prerequisite in the account deletion flow. A user who is the sole owner of one or more organizations cannot delete their platform account until they either transfer ownership of each such organization to another active member, or delete those organizations entirely. This endpoint fulfills the transfer path of that requirement, ensuring continuity of ownership without interrupting organizational data.

If the organization has no other active members, ownership transfer is not possible and the sole owner must instead delete the organization before proceeding with account deletion.

Related operations:
- `DELETE /members/me` (account deletion) — requires this endpoint to be called first if the authenticated user is the sole owner of any organization.
- `DELETE /erpHrm/member/organizations/{organizationId}` — alternative path when there are no other active members to receive ownership.
operations.name: transferOwnership
operations.specification:
1. Authenticate the calling member via their session and resolve their erp_hrm_organization_members record for the given organizationId.
2. Verify the caller holds the Owner role (erp_hrm_roles.is_builtin = true, name = 'Owner') in this organization. If not, reject with 403 Forbidden.
3. Verify the organization (erp_hrm_organizations) exists and is not deleted (deleted_at IS NULL). If not found, reject with 404.
4. From the request body, extract targetMemberId (the erp_hrm_organization_members.id of the intended new owner) and outgoingOwnerRoleId (the erp_hrm_roles.id the former owner will be demoted to).
5. Validate that the target organization member:
   a. Exists in erp_hrm_organization_members for this organizationId.
   b. Has status = 'active'.
   c. Is not already the Owner (i.e., not the same member as the caller).
6. Validate that outgoingOwnerRoleId refers to a valid role in erp_hrm_roles scoped to this organization and is NOT the Owner role.
7. In a single database transaction:
   a. Update the target member's erp_hrm_organization_members.role_id to the Owner role ID.
   b. Update the caller's (former owner's) erp_hrm_organization_members.role_id to outgoingOwnerRoleId.
   c. Update erp_hrm_organizations.owner_member_id to the target member's erp_hrm_members.member_id (the platform-level member reference).
   d. Set updated_at = NOW() on both erp_hrm_organization_members records and the erp_hrm_organization record.
8. Return the updated erp_hrm_organizations record as IErpHrmOrganization.

responseBody.description: The updated organization record reflecting the new owner.

parameters.description: The UUID of the organization whose ownership is being transferred.
parameters.name: organizationId

requestBody.description: Ownership transfer details: the target member to receive the Owner role and the role to assign to the outgoing owner.

prerequisites.description: The organization identified by `organizationId` must exist before its ownership can be transferred. Creating the organization also auto-creates the built-in Owner, Manager, and Employee roles, one of which will serve as the `outgoingOwnerRoleId` for the demoted owner.

A target organization member must exist in the organization before they can receive the Owner role. The `targetMemberId` in the request body references `erp_hrm_organization_members.id`, which is created by this endpoint. The target member must have status='active' and must not already be the Owner.

operations.description:
