Accept a specific pending invitation within the organization, transitioning it from 'pending' to 'accepted' status and adding the invitee as an active organization member.

This operation allows users with the `employee:manage` permission to manually accept a pending invitation on behalf of the organization. When accepted, the system locates the invitation record in `erp_hrm_invitations` by the given `invitationId`, verifies it is in `pending` status, resolves or confirms the linked `erp_hrm_members` account for the invited email address, and creates or confirms an `erp_hrm_organization_members` record to formally add the invitee to the organization. The invitation's `status` field is then updated from `pending` to `accepted` and the `erp_hrm_member_id` is populated with the matching member account.

Access control is strictly enforced: only authenticated members holding the `employee:manage` permission within the organization that owns this invitation may perform this action. Any attempt by an unauthorized actor is rejected. The invitation must belong to the same organization context as the acting member.

The `erp_hrm_invitations` table tracks the full lifecycle of each invitation. The `status` field transitions follow the allowed lifecycle: `pending` → `accepted`. If the invitation is already in a terminal state (`accepted`, `rejected`, `expired`, or `cancelled`), this operation will fail with an appropriate error. Similarly, if no registered `erp_hrm_members` account exists for the invited email address at the time of this call, the operation cannot complete successfully.

Related operations: `POST /organizations/{organizationId}/invitations` to send an initial invitation, `PATCH /invitations` to list and monitor all invitations for an organization, and `GET /invitations/{invitationId}` to retrieve a specific invitation's current status and details.
operations.name: accept
operations.specification:
1. Authenticate the acting member and verify they hold the `employee:manage` permission within the organization context.
2. Query `erp_hrm_invitations` by the provided `invitationId` (UUID primary key). If not found, return 404.
3. Validate that the invitation's `erp_hrm_organization_id` matches the acting member's current organization context. If not, return 403.
4. Check the invitation's `status` field: if it is not `pending`, return a 422 or 409 error indicating the invitation is not in a state that can be accepted.
5. Look up `erp_hrm_members` by the invitation's `email` field. If no active member account exists for that email (i.e., the invitee has not yet registered), return a 422 error — the invitee must register first before this manual acceptance can be applied.
6. In a database transaction:
   a. Update the `erp_hrm_invitations` record: set `status = 'accepted'`, `erp_hrm_member_id = <matched member's id>`, and `updated_at = NOW()`.
   b. Check if an `erp_hrm_organization_members` record already exists for `(organization_id, member_id)`. If not, create a new `erp_hrm_organization_members` record using the organization's default role (e.g., the Employee built-in role) and `employment_type` and `status = 'active'`.
7. Commit the transaction.
8. Return the updated `erp_hrm_invitations` record as `IErpHrmInvitation`, including the linked member and organization details.
9. Emit a real-time invitation accepted event and a member-added event to relevant subscribers per the real-time monitoring requirements.

responseBody.description: The updated invitation record reflecting the accepted status.

parameters.description: The unique UUID identifier of the pending invitation to be accepted.
parameters.name: invitationId

prerequisites.description: An organization must exist before any invitation can be issued or accepted. The invitation is scoped to a specific organization (erp_hrm_invitations.erp_hrm_organization_id), so the organization record must be created first.

A pending invitation must exist with the given invitationId before it can be accepted. This operation creates the erp_hrm_invitations record in 'pending' status that the accept operation looks up. Without a prior invitation, the accept call returns 404.

operations.description:
Switch the authenticated member's active organization context to the specified organization.

This operation enables a member who belongs to multiple organizations to change their active working context. All subsequent API calls made after a successful switch are scoped exclusively to the newly selected organization — including employees, projects, tasks, timelogs, timesheets, departments, and all other organizational data. Data from the previous organization context is no longer visible until the member switches back.

The system validates that the requesting member is currently an active member of the target organization (i.e., a record exists in `erp_hrm_organization_members` with the combination of the caller's member ID and the specified `organizationId`). If the member is not a member of the target organization, or if the target organization has been deleted, the switch is denied and the current organization context remains unchanged (see section 191 of the functional requirements: Switching to an Unjoined Organization Denied).

Upon a successful switch, the server updates the session's active organization context to the target organization. The member's role and permission set are immediately replaced with those defined for their membership record in the newly selected organization. A member holding an Owner role in one organization and an Employee role in another will have full owner-level access in the first context and restricted employee-level access in the second — the switch is instant and complete.

The response returns the caller's `erp_hrm_organization_members` record within the newly selected organization, confirming the new identity, role assignment, employment classification, status, position, and department placement that will govern all subsequent actions in this session.

This endpoint is related to the organization listing endpoint (e.g., GET /organizations) which must be called first to retrieve the list of organizations the member belongs to and to obtain the target `organizationId` to pass here.
operations.name: switchContext
operations.specification:
1. Authenticate the requesting member from the session token.
2. Verify that the target organization (identified by `organizationId`) exists and is not deleted (deleted_at IS NULL) in `erp_hrm_organizations`.
3. Query `erp_hrm_organization_members` for a record matching (organization_id = organizationId AND member_id = callerMemberId AND deleted_at IS NULL). If no such record exists, return 403 Forbidden — the member is not a member of the target organization.
4. Verify the found OrganizationMember has status = 'active'. If 'deactivated', return 403 Forbidden.
5. Update the session's active organization context to the target organizationId. This may be stored in the JWT, a session store, or a session table (erp_hrm_member_sessions is append-only, so a new session token or an in-memory context store approach is appropriate depending on implementation).
6. Load the full OrganizationMember record including its related role (with permissions), department (if any), and member profile.
7. Return the IErpHrmOrganizationMember response DTO representing the caller's membership in the newly selected organization.
8. Edge cases: If organizationId equals the currently active organization, the switch is a no-op but still returns the current OrganizationMember record with 200 OK.

responseBody.description: The authenticated member's OrganizationMember record within the newly selected organization, reflecting the role, permissions, employment type, status, and position now active in the switched context.

parameters.description: The UUID of the target organization to switch into. Must be an organization the authenticated member currently belongs to.
parameters.name: organizationId

prerequisites.description: An organization must exist and the authenticated member must be an active member of it before the context switch can succeed. Creating an organization via this endpoint automatically establishes the creator as an active Owner-role member, providing the valid organizationId needed for the switch and satisfying the membership existence check performed by the switch operation.

operations.description:
Deactivate an active organization member, immediately restricting their ability to perform work within the organization.

This operation transitions the target organization member's status from `active` to `deactivated` within the `erp_hrm_organization_members` table. Once deactivated, the member is immediately prevented from creating new timelogs, submitting or modifying timesheets, and starting or stopping timers. All existing historical records — timelogs, timesheets, contracts, task assignments — are fully preserved and remain accessible to users with appropriate view permissions.

The requesting actor must hold the `employee:manage` permission within the same organization as the target member. If the requester lacks this permission, the system rejects the request with a permission denied error. Additionally, the sole owner of an organization cannot be deactivated through this flow; ownership transfer must occur first before deactivation can proceed.

A deactivated member remains visible in the employee list and continues to appear in search and filter results. Their user account remains active for any other organizations they belong to — deactivation is strictly scoped to the target organization. This action is recorded as an entry in the `erp_hrm_activity_logs` table for auditing purposes, with action_type `employee_deactivated` and target_entity_type `member`.

The member's `department_id`, `position`, `employment_type`, and `role_id` assignments in `erp_hrm_organization_members` are all preserved unchanged. Reactivation is possible at any time via the corresponding reactivate endpoint, which restores full work capabilities.

Related operations:
- `POST /erpHrm/member/organizationMembers/{organizationMemberId}/reactivate` — Reactivates a previously deactivated member, restoring all time-tracking and timesheet capabilities.
- `PATCH /erpHrm/member/organizationMembers` — Lists and searches organization members, including deactivated ones via status filter.
operations.name: deactivate
operations.specification:
1. **Authentication & Authorization**: Verify the requesting actor is an authenticated member. Extract their organization context from the session. Confirm the actor's role has the `employee:manage` permission code assigned via erp_hrm_role_permissions. If not, return 403 Forbidden.

2. **Target Lookup**: Query erp_hrm_organization_members by the provided `organizationMemberId` (UUID). Ensure the record exists and belongs to the same organization as the requesting actor. If not found or mismatched organization, return 404 Not Found.

3. **Status Guard**: Check that the target member's current `status` is `'active'`. If already `'deactivated'`, return a 409 Conflict or a business error indicating the member is already deactivated.

4. **Owner Guard**: Determine if the target member is the sole owner of the organization. Join with erp_hrm_roles to check if the target has the built-in Owner role. Count how many active members share the Owner role. If the target is the only owner, reject the request with a business error stating ownership must be transferred first.

5. **Status Update**: Update erp_hrm_organization_members.status to `'deactivated'` and set `updated_at` to the current timestamp for the target record.

6. **Active Timer Termination**: Query erp_hrm_timers for any active timer belonging to this organization member. If one exists, stop it (e.g., set its end state or remove it) to enforce that a deactivated member cannot have an active timer.

7. **Activity Log**: Insert a new entry into erp_hrm_activity_logs recording the deactivation action, referencing the performing organization member's ID and the target member's ID.

8. **Response**: Return the updated erp_hrm_organization_members record mapped to IErpHrmOrganizationMember, with status reflecting `'deactivated'`.

9. **Error Handling**: Handle the following edge cases explicitly:
   - 404: Target member not found or outside requester's organization
   - 403: Requester lacks `employee:manage` permission
   - 409: Member is already deactivated
   - 422: Target is the sole owner — ownership must be transferred first

responseBody.description: The updated organization member record reflecting the deactivated status.

parameters.description: The UUID of the organization member record to deactivate. References erp_hrm_organization_members.id.
parameters.name: organizationMemberId

prerequisites.description: An organization member record must exist and be in 'active' status before it can be deactivated. This prerequisite creates the organization member identified by `organizationMemberId` that the deactivation operation will target. Without this, the lookup in step 2 of the deactivation flow returns 404 Not Found.

operations.description:
Reactivate a deactivated organization member, restoring their ability to perform work within the organization.

This operation transitions an organization member's status from `deactivated` back to `active` within the `erp_hrm_organization_members` table. Once reactivated, the member immediately regains the ability to create timelogs, start timers, and submit timesheets. No additional setup is required after reactivation.

Only users who hold the `employee:manage` permission within the organization may perform this action. Attempting to reactivate a member without this permission will result in a permission denied error. This permission is governed by the member's assigned role in `erp_hrm_roles`.

The operation affects only the `status` field of the target `erp_hrm_organization_members` record, changing it from `deactivated` to `active` and updating the `updated_at` timestamp accordingly. All other fields — including `role_id`, `department_id`, `position`, `employment_type`, and `created_at` — remain completely unchanged.

All historical records attributed to the member — including past timelogs (`erp_hrm_timelogs`), timesheets (`erp_hrm_timesheets`), employment contracts (`erp_hrm_employee_contracts`), project memberships (`erp_hrm_project_members`), and task assignments (`erp_hrm_tasks`) — are fully preserved throughout the deactivation and reactivation cycle. No data loss occurs during either transition.

This endpoint may only be called on a member record that is currently in the `deactivated` status. If the target member is already `active`, the operation will return an error. The same member may be deactivated and reactivated multiple times over their tenure in the organization.

To view the current status of an organization member before reactivating, use `GET /erpHrm/member/organizationMembers/{organizationMemberId}`. To change a member's status to deactivated, use the corresponding member deactivation endpoint. Reactivation events are recorded in the organization's activity log (`erp_hrm_activity_logs`).
operations.name: reactivate
operations.specification:
1. Authenticate the requesting member session and resolve their organization context.
2. Verify that the requesting member holds the `employee:manage` permission (check their role's permissions in `erp_hrm_role_permissions`).
3. Load the target `erp_hrm_organization_members` record by `id = organizationMemberId`. Ensure the record exists and `deleted_at IS NULL`.
4. Confirm that the target member's `status` is `deactivated`. If it is already `active`, return a 409 Conflict or 400 Bad Request error indicating the member is not in a deactivated state.
5. Ensure the target member belongs to the same organization as the requesting member (compare `organization_id`).
6. Update the target record: set `status = 'active'` and `updated_at = NOW()`.
7. Persist the change in a database transaction.
8. Create an entry in `erp_hrm_activity_logs` recording the reactivation event, referencing the acting member and the target member.
9. Return the full updated `erp_hrm_organization_members` record including joined relations (role, department, member/user profile details) as the `IErpHrmOrganizationMember` response type.
10. Edge cases:
    - Target member not found or deleted → 404 Not Found
    - Requesting member lacks `employee:manage` permission → 403 Forbidden
    - Target member is already active → 400 Bad Request
    - Target member belongs to a different organization → 403 Forbidden or 404 Not Found

responseBody.description: The updated organization member record reflecting the restored active status.

parameters.description: The UUID of the organization member record to reactivate. Must reference a currently deactivated member within the organization.
parameters.name: organizationMemberId

prerequisites.description: An organization member record identified by organizationMemberId must exist before it can be reactivated. This POST call creates the member record whose UUID is then used as the path parameter. Without an existing member record, the reactivation endpoint returns 404 Not Found.

The target organization member must be in 'deactivated' status before this reactivation endpoint can succeed. This deactivation call transitions the member from 'active' to 'deactivated', which is the required precondition. If the member is already active, the reactivation endpoint returns 400 Bad Request.

operations.description:
Stop an active timer and automatically create a timelog from the elapsed session.

This operation terminates the authenticated member's active timer session identified by `timerId`. Upon invocation, the system calculates the total elapsed duration from the timer's `started_at` timestamp to the moment the stop action is taken. The duration is rounded to the nearest whole minute (e.g., 7 minutes 29 seconds → 7 minutes; 7 minutes 30 seconds → 8 minutes), consistent with the rounding rules defined for the `duration_minutes` field in `erp_hrm_timelogs`.

If the rounded duration is greater than zero, the system automatically creates a new `erp_hrm_timelogs` record on behalf of the member. The newly created timelog inherits the `project_id`, `task_id`, and `description` from the timer at the moment of stopping. The `work_date` is set to the calendar date of the stop action, and `billable` defaults to `true`. The timer record in `erp_hrm_timers` is then permanently removed since timers are transient records that exist only to facilitate real-time tracking.

If the elapsed time rounds to zero minutes (i.e., the timer was stopped almost immediately after starting), the system does not create a timelog. The operation is rejected or treated as equivalent to discarding the timer, and the caller is informed that the elapsed time was insufficient to record.

Access control is enforced at the service layer: only the owner of the timer (the `organization_member_id` associated with the timer) may call this endpoint. Members holding the time management permission may stop any employee's active timer on their behalf.

This operation depends on the existence of an active timer. To verify or retrieve the current state of the active timer before stopping it, use `GET /timers/{timerId}`. After the timelog is created, it follows its own independent lifecycle and may be submitted as part of a weekly timesheet via the Timesheet endpoints.
operations.name: stop
operations.specification:
1. Authenticate the calling member and resolve their organization_member_id from the session.
2. Look up the timer record in erp_hrm_timers by the given timerId (UUID). If not found, return 404.
3. Authorization check: verify that either (a) the timer's organization_member_id matches the calling member's organization_member_id, or (b) the calling member holds the time management permission within the same organization. If neither condition is met, return 403.
4. Compute elapsed duration: subtract started_at from the current UTC timestamp to get total seconds. Convert to minutes using standard rounding (round half up): Math.round(totalSeconds / 60). Store as duration_minutes.
5. If duration_minutes === 0: do NOT create a timelog. Return an error response (e.g., 422 Unprocessable Entity) indicating the elapsed time was too short to record. Do not delete the timer in this case — or treat it as a discard (implementation decision based on UX requirements; typically reject without deleting).
6. If duration_minutes > 0:
   a. Begin a database transaction.
   b. Insert a new row into erp_hrm_timelogs with:
      - id: new UUID
      - organization_member_id: from the timer
      - project_id: from the timer
      - task_id: from the timer (nullable)
      - timesheet_id: null (not yet assigned to any timesheet)
      - work_date: current UTC date (midnight UTC of the stop timestamp)
      - duration_minutes: calculated value
      - billable: true (default)
      - description: from the timer (nullable)
      - created_at: current UTC timestamp
      - updated_at: current UTC timestamp
   c. Delete the timer record from erp_hrm_timers by timerId.
   d. Commit the transaction.
7. Return the newly created erp_hrm_timelogs record as IErpHrmTimelog.
8. Edge cases:
   - If the timer is not active (already stopped/deleted concurrently), return 404 or 409.
   - Wrap the insert + delete in a transaction to ensure atomicity; if either step fails, roll back and return 500.
   - Do not allow this endpoint to be called for a timer belonging to a different organization than the calling member's active organization context.

responseBody.description: The newly created timelog record produced from the stopped timer, containing the calculated duration, inherited project, task, and description.

parameters.description: The UUID of the active timer to stop. Must be an existing active timer record in erp_hrm_timers.
parameters.name: timerId

prerequisites.description: An active timer must exist before it can be stopped. The timer is created via POST /erpHrm/member/timers, which returns the timerId required as a path parameter for this stop operation. Without a previously started timer, the stop request will fail with 404.

operations.description:
Submit a draft timesheet for managerial review and approval, transitioning its status from 'draft' to 'submitted'.

This operation is the formal act through which an employee presents their weekly time records to a reviewer. Once submitted, the timesheet enters the 'submitted' state and cannot be modified by the employee until the reviewer either approves it (locking it permanently) or rejects it (returning it to 'draft' for revision). The submission timestamp (`submitted_at`) is recorded upon this action.

The target timesheet is identified by its UUID (`timesheetId`). The authenticated member must be the owner of the timesheet; submission on behalf of other employees is not permitted. Additionally, the member must currently be in 'active' status — deactivated members are blocked from initiating new work-related actions, including timesheet submission.

Several validation rules are enforced before the status transition is allowed. First, the timesheet must be in 'draft' status; a timesheet already in 'submitted' or 'approved' state cannot be re-submitted. Second, the timesheet must contain at least one timelog (`erp_hrm_timelogs` rows linked via `timesheet_id`); an empty timesheet cannot be submitted. Third, no other timesheet belonging to the same employee and covering the same calendar week may currently be in 'submitted' or 'approved' status — only one active submission per week per employee is allowed. Fourth, every timelog included in the timesheet must have a `work_date` that falls within the timesheet's defined week (`week_start_date` to `week_end_date`); timelogs outside the week range will cause the submission to be rejected.

The `erp_hrm_timesheets` table stores the weekly boundaries as `week_start_date` (Monday) and `week_end_date` (Sunday), enforced by the unique constraint on `(organization_member_id, week_start_date)`. The `status` field reflects the current position in the lifecycle: draft → submitted → approved or rejected.

After a successful submission, the caller receives the full updated timesheet entity, including the newly set `status` ('submitted') and `submitted_at` timestamp. Clients should use this response to update the local state of the timesheet display. To view the list of timesheets or check their current state prior to submission, use `PATCH /timesheets` (the index operation). To approve or reject a submitted timesheet, users with the `time:approve` permission use the respective approve or reject endpoints.
operations.name: submit
operations.specification:
1. Authenticate the calling member from the session context and resolve their active OrganizationMember record.
2. Look up the erp_hrm_timesheets row by the provided timesheetId. If not found, return 404.
3. Verify that the timesheet's organization_member_id matches the authenticated member's OrganizationMember id. If not, return 403.
4. Check the OrganizationMember's status field; if it is 'deactivated', reject the submission with an appropriate error.
5. Verify the timesheet's current status is 'draft'. If it is 'submitted' or 'approved', reject with a conflict error explaining the timesheet is not in a revisable state.
6. Count the number of erp_hrm_timelogs rows where timesheet_id = timesheetId. If the count is 0, reject the request — a timesheet must contain at least one timelog before it can be submitted.
7. Check for duplicate-week conflict: query erp_hrm_timesheets for any row where organization_member_id = current member's id AND week_start_date = this timesheet's week_start_date AND status IN ('submitted', 'approved') AND id != timesheetId. If such a row exists, reject the submission.
8. Optionally verify that all timelogs linked to this timesheet have a work_date falling within [week_start_date, week_end_date]. If any timelog falls outside the week range, reject the submission.
9. Within a database transaction, update erp_hrm_timesheets: set status = 'submitted', submitted_at = now(), updated_at = now().
10. Return the full timesheet record including all updated fields.

responseBody.description: The updated timesheet record reflecting the newly submitted status.

parameters.description: The UUID of the timesheet to be submitted for review.
parameters.name: timesheetId

prerequisites.description: A draft timesheet must be created first to obtain the `timesheetId` used in this operation's path. The submit operation looks up the timesheet by this UUID and returns 404 if it does not exist.

At least one timelog must be created and linked to the draft timesheet before submission. The submit operation enforces a business rule that rejects any timesheet containing zero timelogs, returning an error and leaving the timesheet in 'draft' status.

operations.description:
Approve a submitted timesheet on behalf of an authorized reviewer.

This operation transitions the target timesheet from `submitted` status to `approved` status. It is exclusively available to organization members who hold the `time:approve` permission within the organization. Once approved, the timesheet's `reviewer_id` is set to the acting member, and the `reviewed_at` timestamp is recorded to form a clear audit trail as defined in the `erp_hrm_timesheets` schema.

The timesheet must be in `submitted` status for this action to succeed. If the timesheet is still in `draft` status, already in `approved` status, or in `rejected` status (returned to draft for revision), the request is rejected. Only timesheets actively awaiting review can be approved.

The acting member must hold the `time:approve` permission in the organization that owns the timesheet. Members without this permission are denied, regardless of any other roles or permissions they may hold. This permission check is enforced on every approval request.

Self-approval is strictly prohibited. Even if the acting member holds `time:approve` permission, they may not approve a timesheet for which they are the owner (`organization_member_id`). The system compares the identity of the acting member with the timesheet owner and denies the request if they match.

Upon successful approval, the system updates the `status` column to `approved`, sets `reviewer_id` to the acting organization member's ID, and records the current timestamp in `reviewed_at`. The fully updated `erp_hrm_timesheets` record is returned to the caller.

Related operations: Use `PATCH /timesheets` to browse and filter timesheets awaiting approval. Use `POST /timesheets/{timesheetId}/reject` to reject a submitted timesheet instead. Use `GET /timesheets/{timesheetId}` to retrieve the current state of a timesheet before taking action.
operations.name: approve
operations.specification:
1. Authenticate the acting member from the session and resolve their organization membership record (`erp_hrm_organization_members`).
2. Load the target timesheet from `erp_hrm_timesheets` by `timesheetId` (UUID). If not found, return 404.
3. Verify the timesheet belongs to the same organization as the acting member. If not, return 403.
4. Check that the acting member's role has the `time:approve` permission by querying `erp_hrm_role_permissions`. If missing, return 403.
5. Compare the acting member's `id` with the timesheet's `organization_member_id`. If they match (self-approval), return 403.
6. Verify the timesheet `status` is exactly `'submitted'`. If it is `'draft'`, `'approved'`, or `'rejected'`, return 422 with an appropriate error message.
7. Within a database transaction:
   a. Update `erp_hrm_timesheets` SET `status = 'approved'`, `reviewer_id = <acting_member_id>`, `reviewed_at = NOW()`, `updated_at = NOW()` WHERE `id = timesheetId`.
8. Reload the updated timesheet record with associated relations (owner member, reviewer member, timelogs) and return it as `IErpHrmTimesheet`.
9. Edge cases:
   - Concurrent approval attempts: rely on the status check within the transaction to prevent double-processing.
   - Deactivated reviewer: if the acting member's `status` is `'deactivated'`, treat as unauthorized (403).

responseBody.description: The fully updated timesheet record reflecting the approved status, the reviewer identity, and the review timestamp.

parameters.description: The UUID of the target timesheet to approve. The timesheet must be in submitted status and must not be owned by the acting reviewer.
parameters.name: timesheetId

prerequisites.description: A timesheet record identified by timesheetId must exist in erp_hrm_timesheets before it can be approved. If no timesheet with the given UUID exists, the approval operation returns 404.

The timesheet must be in 'submitted' status before it can be approved. Calling the submit endpoint transitions the timesheet from 'draft' to 'submitted'. If the timesheet is not in 'submitted' status (e.g., still draft, already approved, or rejected/returned to draft), the approval request is rejected with 422.

operations.description:
Reject a submitted timesheet on behalf of an authorized reviewer, returning it to draft status with a mandatory written reason.

This operation allows organization members who hold the `time:approve` permission to reject a timesheet that is currently in the `submitted` status. Upon successful rejection, the timesheet's `status` is transitioned back to `draft`, the `reviewer_id` is set to the acting reviewer's organization member ID, the `reviewed_at` timestamp is recorded, and the provided `rejection_reason` is persisted on the record.

Access is strictly restricted to members with the `time:approve` permission within the organization. Members without this permission — regardless of their role or any other permissions they hold — will have their request denied. Additionally, reviewers cannot act on their own timesheets; self-rejection is not permitted.

A non-empty `rejection_reason` is required. If the caller omits or provides a blank reason, the system rejects the request and the timesheet remains in `submitted` status unchanged. This ensures employees always receive actionable feedback explaining what must be corrected before resubmission.

The timesheet must be in `submitted` status. Attempting to reject a timesheet that is in `draft`, `approved`, or already `rejected` status will result in an error without any state change.

After rejection, the timesheet returns to `draft` status, unlocking its associated timelogs so the employee may edit them. The employee may then add or remove timelogs before resubmitting, following the same submission rules (at least one timelog, all timelogs within the same calendar week, no duplicate submitted or approved timesheets for the same week).

Related operations: `PATCH /timesheets` to browse timesheets, `GET /timesheets/{timesheetId}` to retrieve a specific timesheet, `POST /timesheets/{timesheetId}/approve` to approve a submitted timesheet, and `POST /timesheets/{timesheetId}/submit` for the employee to submit a draft timesheet.
operations.name: reject
operations.specification:
1. Authenticate the calling member session and resolve their current organization context.
2. Load the target timesheet from `erp_hrm_timesheets` by the provided `timesheetId`. Return 404 if not found.
3. Verify that the timesheet belongs to the same organization as the calling reviewer (via `organization_member_id` → `erp_hrm_organization_members.organization_id`).
4. Check that the calling member's role has the `time:approve` permission by querying `erp_hrm_role_permissions`. Return 403 if not granted.
5. Ensure the timesheet `status` is exactly `submitted`. Return 422 with an appropriate error message if it is `draft`, `approved`, or `rejected`.
6. Validate that `rejection_reason` in the request body is non-null and non-empty (after trimming whitespace). Return 422 if the reason is missing or blank.
7. In a single database transaction:
   a. Update `erp_hrm_timesheets` SET `status` = 'rejected', `reviewer_id` = (calling reviewer's organization_member id), `reviewed_at` = NOW(), `rejection_reason` = (provided reason), `updated_at` = NOW() WHERE `id` = `timesheetId`.
   b. No changes are needed to individual timelogs at this step; locking/unlocking is managed by the submission/approval lifecycle.
8. Return the fully populated `IErpHrmTimesheet` record including owner, reviewer details, all timestamps, and the stored rejection_reason.

responseBody.description: The updated timesheet record reflecting the rejected status, reviewer identity, review timestamp, and rejection reason.

parameters.description: The UUID of the timesheet to reject. The timesheet must be in 'submitted' status.
parameters.name: timesheetId

requestBody.description: Rejection details including the mandatory written reason for declining the timesheet.

prerequisites.description: A timesheet record must be created before it can be rejected. The {timesheetId} path parameter must reference an existing timesheet in the database; without it the reject operation returns 404.

The timesheet must be in 'submitted' status before it can be rejected. This submit operation transitions the timesheet from 'draft' to 'submitted'. Attempting to reject a timesheet that is not in 'submitted' status results in a 422 error.

authorizations.name: guest
authorizations.description: Unauthenticated visitors who can register a new account (and optionally create an organization during sign-up) or log in with email and password.

authorizations.name: member
authorizations.description: Authenticated users who belong to one or more organizations. Within each organization they hold exactly one role (Owner, Manager, Employee, or a custom role) that governs their permissions. They can switch organization context, manage their profile, track time, and perform any action permitted by their current organization role.

current.description:
Current page number being viewed (1-indexed).

Indicates which page of results is currently being returned. Page
numbering starts from 1, so the first page is page 1 (not 0). This value
reflects the page parameter from the request after validation and bounds
checking.

limit.description:
Maximum number of records per page.

Defines the upper bound on how many records can be returned in a single
page. This corresponds to the limit parameter from the request. The
actual number of records in the data array may be less than this value on
the final page or when total records are fewer than the limit.
limit.x-autobe-specification: Maximum records per page. Actual count may be less on last page.

records.description:
Total count of all records matching the query criteria.

Represents the complete number of records available across all pages, not
just the current page. This value is computed via a COUNT query and is
essential for calculating total pages and displaying pagination UI
elements like "Showing 1-10 of 150 results".
records.x-autobe-specification: Total record count across all pages.

pages.description:
Total number of pages available.

Calculated as ceiling of {@link records} divided by {@link limit}. When
records is 0, pages will also be 0. This value enables clients to render
page navigation controls and validate page bounds.
pages.x-autobe-specification: Total pages. Calculated as Math.ceil(records / limit).

IPage.IPagination.description:
Pagination metadata containing current page position and total data
statistics.

This interface provides comprehensive pagination information returned
alongside paginated list data. It enables clients to implement navigation
controls, display progress indicators, and determine data boundaries for UI
rendering.
IPage.IPagination.x-autobe-specification: Pagination metadata for paginated list responses. Included in all list endpoint responses.

access.description:
Short-lived JWT access token for authenticating API requests.

This token must be included in the Authorization header using the Bearer
scheme (e.g., `Authorization: Bearer {access}`) for all endpoints requiring
authentication. The token contains encoded claims including user identity,
roles, and permissions. Typically expires within 15-60 minutes for
security; use the refresh token to obtain a new access token when expired.
access.x-autobe-specification: JWT access token. Use in Authorization header as "Bearer {access}".

refresh.description:
Long-lived refresh token for obtaining new access tokens.

Used to request new access tokens when the current access token expires,
allowing session continuation without re-authentication. Should be stored
securely and transmitted only to the token refresh endpoint. Typical
lifetime ranges from 7 to 30 days depending on security requirements.
refresh.x-autobe-specification: Refresh token for obtaining new access tokens without re-authentication.

expired_at.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp when the access token expires.

After this timestamp, the access token will be rejected by authenticated
endpoints. Clients should proactively refresh before expiration to maintain
seamless user experience. A common strategy is to refresh when remaining
time falls below 5 minutes. This timestamp is also embedded within the JWT
itself as the "exp" claim.
expired_at.x-autobe-specification: Access token expiration timestamp in ISO 8601 format.

refreshable_until.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp indicating the absolute session expiration deadline.

Represents the latest possible time the refresh token can be used. Once
this timestamp is reached, the user must fully re-authenticate with
credentials. This defines the maximum session duration regardless of
activity. If refresh token rotation is enabled, this deadline may extend
with each successful refresh.

refresh.description: The JWT refresh token previously received from a login or token refresh response. Submit this token to obtain a new access and refresh token pair, extending the session without re-entering credentials.
refresh.x-autobe-specification: The JWT refresh token string previously issued by the login (POST /erpHrm/auth/member/login) or a prior token refresh (POST /erpHrm/auth/member/refresh) endpoint. On receipt: 1) Verify the JWT signature. 2) Extract claims: erp_hrm_members.id and erp_hrm_member_sessions.id. 3) Query erp_hrm_member_sessions WHERE id = session_id from claims — return 401 if not found. 4) Check erp_hrm_member_sessions.expired_at > NOW() — return 401 if expired. 5) Load erp_hrm_members record, verify deleted_at IS NULL — return 401 if deleted. On success, update or replace the session record and issue a new token pair.

IErpHrmMember.IRefresh.description: Request body for renewing an authenticated member's session. Submit the refresh token previously issued at login or the last token refresh. The server validates the token signature and session validity, then returns a new JWT access and refresh token pair without requiring the member to re-enter their credentials.
IErpHrmMember.IRefresh.x-autobe-specification: This is a request payload DTO used exclusively by the POST /erpHrm/auth/member/refresh endpoint. It contains the JWT refresh token previously issued upon member login or a prior token refresh. Implementation: the `refresh` field value is validated as a JWT — verify signature, decode claims (member id, session id), query erp_hrm_member_sessions WHERE id = session_id AND expired_at > NOW(), verify the associated erp_hrm_members.deleted_at IS NULL. If all checks pass, invalidate the old session and issue a new token pair. If any check fails, return 401 Unauthorized.

email.description: The registered email address of the member account used as the login identifier. Must match an existing, non-deactivated account.
email.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping to erp_hrm_members.email. The server queries: SELECT * FROM erp_hrm_members WHERE email = :email AND deleted_at IS NULL. Must be a valid email format. Unique at the platform level.

password.description: The member's plaintext password for credential verification. The server validates this against the securely stored bcrypt hash. This value is never stored or returned.
password.x-autobe-specification: Maps to erp_hrm_members.password_hash via bcrypt verification. The client submits the plaintext password; the server calls bcrypt.verify(password, password_hash). The raw hash is never returned to the client. If verification fails, a 401 is returned with the same message as 'email not found' to prevent enumeration.

IErpHrmMember.ILogin.description: Request body for authenticating an existing member via email and password credentials. The `email` field must match a registered, non-deactivated member account. The `password` field is the member's plaintext password, which the server verifies against the stored bcrypt hash. Neither the failure reason nor whether an email exists is revealed in error responses, protecting against user enumeration attacks.
IErpHrmMember.ILogin.x-autobe-specification: This is the request body DTO for POST /erpHrm/auth/member/login. The server uses `email` to look up erp_hrm_members WHERE email = :email AND deleted_at IS NULL. The `password` field is the plaintext password provided by the user; the server verifies it against erp_hrm_members.password_hash using bcrypt. If the email is not found, the account is soft-deleted, or the password does not match, a 401 Unauthorized is returned without distinguishing between failure reasons (enumeration protection). Session context (ip, href, referrer) is captured server-side from the HTTP request and is NOT part of this DTO.

permission_code.description: The permission code to grant to the target custom role. Must be one of the predefined permission codes that control access to specific categories of actions within the organization. Each code represents a distinct capability area and can be combined freely on a custom role.
permission_code.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping to erp_hrm_role_permissions.permission_code. Must be exactly one of the 9 allowed constant values: 'org:manage', 'employee:manage', 'employee:view', 'project:manage', 'project:view', 'time:manage', 'time:approve', 'time:view_all', 'report:view'. Validate against this set before inserting. Return 400 Bad Request for any value not in the allowed set. The (role_id, permission_code) combination must be unique; return 409 Conflict if the role already holds this permission code.

IErpHrmRolePermission.ICreate.description:
Request body for adding a single permission code to a custom role within an organization.

The caller supplies exactly one permission code from the predefined set of available codes. Each code unlocks a specific category of actions within the organization. The target role (identified by the path parameter `roleId`) must be a custom role — built-in roles (Owner, Manager, Employee) cannot have their permissions modified via this endpoint.

Available permission codes:
- `org:manage` — manage organization settings
- `employee:manage` — manage employee records
- `employee:view` — view employee records
- `project:manage` — manage projects
- `project:view` — view projects
- `time:manage` — manage time entries
- `time:approve` — approve timesheets
- `time:view_all` — view all members' time entries
- `report:view` — view reports

Duplicate grants (adding a permission code the role already holds) are rejected with a 409 Conflict response.

The caller provides only one field: `permission_code`, which must be one of the 9 predefined string constants. The `id` is auto-generated as a UUID server-side. The `role_id` is resolved from the `roleId` path parameter. The `created_at` is set to the current server timestamp at insert time. The `role` relation is not included in this request body. Validate `permission_code` against the allowed set before inserting. Reject duplicate (role_id, permission_code) pairs with 409 Conflict.

An invalid, malformed, expired, or orphaned token results in a 401 Unauthorized response. No direct DB column mapping — this is a server-issued opaque credential.

The refresh token encodes the guest's session identity, so no additional identifying fields are required.

IErpHrmMemberSession.IRequest.description:
Search criteria and pagination parameters for filtering and paginating member session records.

All fields are optional. When omitted, all sessions belonging to the authenticated member are returned, ordered by creation date descending. Use `isActive` to restrict results to currently valid (unexpired) or already-expired sessions. Use `ip` for a partial-text search on the client IP address recorded at login time. 2. isActive: true → WHERE expired_at > NOW(); false → WHERE expired_at <= NOW(); omitted → no filter on expiry.

IErpHrmOrganizationMember.IRequest.description: Request body for retrieving a filtered and paginated list of organization members. All fields are optional. This DTO is used to filter and paginate erp_hrm_organization_members records scoped to the current organization (resolved from session). Apply all provided filters as AND conditions against the erp_hrm_organization_members table:
- status: WHERE status = request.status; allowed values: 'active', 'deactivated'
- employment_type: WHERE employment_type = request.employment_type; allowed values: 'full-time', 'part-time', 'contractor', 'intern'
- department_id: WHERE department_id = request.department_id (UUID FK to erp_hrm_departments.id)
- role_id: WHERE role_id = request.role_id (UUID FK to erp_hrm_roles.id)
- keyword: trigram search on erp_hrm_organization_members.position column via GIN index (ILIKE '%keyword%'); also JOIN erp_hrm_members ON member_id and match email (ILIKE '%keyword%'); OR condition within keyword, AND with all other filters
- page: 1-based offset pagination page number, default=1
- limit: page size, default=20, max=100
- sort: sort order string, default='created_at_desc'; allowed values: 'created_at_asc', 'created_at_desc', 'status_asc', 'status_desc', 'employment_type_asc', 'employment_type_desc', 'position_asc', 'position_desc'

keyword.description: Optional keyword for partial name filtering. When provided, only departments whose name contains the given text (case-insensitive) are returned. Omit or pass null to skip name filtering.
keyword.x-autobe-specification: Optional partial-name search filter. When provided (non-null), apply a case-insensitive trigram similarity or ilike match against the erp_hrm_departments.name column using the GIN trigram index (name gin_trgm_ops). When null or omitted, no name filter is applied. Example SQL: WHERE name ILIKE '%:keyword%' or using similarity().

Validate that the provided UUID, if given, references an existing non-deleted department within the same organization.

sortBy.x-autobe-specification: Optional sort column selector. Maps to ORDER BY clause: 'createdAt' → ORDER BY created_at ASC; 'name' → ORDER BY name ASC. When null or omitted, defaults to ORDER BY created_at ASC. Only ascending order is supported for both options.

page.description: The page number to retrieve (1-indexed). The first page is page 1. Defaults to 1 when not specified.
page.x-autobe-specification: 1-indexed page number for pagination. Computes SQL OFFSET as (page - 1) * limit. Minimum value is 1. Defaults to 1 when omitted. Used together with 'limit' to slice the result set.

limit.description: The maximum number of departments to return per page. Must be between 1 and 100. Defaults to 20 when not specified.
limit.x-autobe-specification: Number of department records to return per page. Used as the SQL LIMIT value. Minimum is 1, maximum is 100. Defaults to 20 when omitted. Used together with 'page' to paginate results.

IErpHrmDepartment.IRequest.description:
Request body for searching and paginating the list of departments within a specific organization.

All fields are optional. When omitted, the endpoint returns all active (non-deleted) departments in the organization ordered by creation date with default pagination settings.

The `keyword` field enables partial name matching against department names. The `parentId` field filters departments by their parent: provide a UUID to retrieve direct children of that parent department, provide `null` to retrieve only top-level (root) departments, or omit the field entirely to retrieve departments at all hierarchy levels.

Use `page` and `limit` to control pagination, and `sortBy` to select the sort order.
IErpHrmDepartment.IRequest.x-autobe-specification: This DTO provides optional filter and pagination parameters for querying active (non-deleted) departments from the erp_hrm_departments table scoped to a specific organization. Implementation: (1) 'keyword' applies a GIN trigram or ilike partial match against the 'name' column. (2) 'parentId' filters by 'parent_id': if a UUID string is given, WHERE parent_id = :parentId; if null is given, WHERE parent_id IS NULL (top-level departments only); if the field is omitted entirely, no parent filter is applied. (3) 'sortBy' selects the ORDER BY column: 'createdAt' → ORDER BY created_at ASC (default), 'name' → ORDER BY name ASC; null means use default. (4) 'page' is the 1-indexed page number (default 1). (5) 'limit' is the number of records per page (default 20, max 100). All fields are optional — omitting them all returns all active departments with default ordering and pagination. The organization_id scope is provided via the path parameter, not this DTO.

IErpHrmMember.IJoin.description:
Request body for registering a new member account on the ERP HRM platform.

The registering user provides their email address (which must be globally unique across the platform) and a plain-text password (which is securely hashed server-side using bcrypt before storage). If the email address is already associated with an existing account, the server returns a 409 Conflict error.

Additionally, session context fields (`href`, `referrer`, and optionally `ip`) are captured at registration time to initialize the member's first session record. This allows the system to track the originating page and referrer for audit and security purposes. The `ip` field is optional to accommodate server-side rendering scenarios where the client IP may not be directly available.
IErpHrmMember.IJoin.x-autobe-specification: This DTO represents the request body for the POST /erpHrm/auth/member/join endpoint. Implementation steps: (1) Validate email format and check uniqueness against erp_hrm_members.email — 409 Conflict if already exists. (2) Validate password strength server-side. (3) Hash the provided plain-text password using bcrypt and store in erp_hrm_members.password_hash. (4) INSERT a new row into erp_hrm_members with a generated UUID id, the email, the bcrypt hash, and current timestamps for created_at and updated_at (deleted_at = null). (5) Capture href, referrer, and ip as session context and INSERT a new erp_hrm_member_sessions record (ip falls back to server-detected IP if the client does not supply it). (6) Resolve any pending invitations matching this email and auto-create erp_hrm_organization_members records for each. (7) Issue JWT access + refresh tokens and return IErpHrmMember.IAuthorized.

IErpHrmGuest.IJoin.description: Request body for the guest join operation. Supplies the device fingerprint that uniquely identifies the unauthenticated visitor and the session context (page URL, referrer, and optional client IP) used to create a new guest session record. Guests use this endpoint as their platform entry point before registering or logging in as a member.

The fingerprint field maps to erp_hrm_guests.fingerprint and is used to upsert the guest record (unique index lookup). If an erp_hrm_guests row with that fingerprint exists, it is reused; otherwise a new row is inserted with a new UUID, the given fingerprint, and current timestamps. After the guest record is resolved, a new erp_hrm_guest_sessions row is always inserted: href → guest_sessions.href, referrer → guest_sessions.referrer, ip → guest_sessions.ip (falls back to server-extracted request IP if null). id, created_at, and updated_at on the guest record are auto-generated server-side and are not accepted from the client.

Each code grants the role access to a specific category of organizational actions. IErpHrmRole.description:
Represents a complete role entity within an organization in the ERP HRM system.

A role is a named set of permission codes that defines what an organization member is authorized to do within their organization. Every organization automatically has three built-in roles — Owner, Manager, and Employee — which are system-defined and cannot be deleted or fundamentally altered. The `permissions` array contains the full list of permission code entries assigned to this role, drawn from the `erp_hrm_role_permissions` table. Permission codes govern access to specific organizational capabilities such as managing employees, approving timesheets, or viewing reports.

Roles are strictly scoped to a single organization identified by `organizationId`. A role defined in one organization is never visible or accessible from any other organization context.

IErpHrmRolePermission.IUpdate.description: Request body for atomically replacing the complete set of permission codes assigned to a custom role within an organization. The supplied array fully replaces the role's existing permissions in a single transaction. Providing an empty array removes all permissions. Each element must be one of the nine recognized permission codes: `org:manage`, `employee:manage`, `employee:view`, `project:manage`, `project:view`, `time:manage`, `time:approve`, `time:view_all`, and `report:view`. Duplicate codes are not permitted. The new permissions take effect immediately for all members currently assigned to the role. Only organization owners may invoke this operation; built-in roles (Owner, Manager, Employee) cannot be modified.
IErpHrmRolePermission.IUpdate.x-autobe-specification: This DTO is used as the request body for PATCH /erpHrm/member/organizations/{organizationId}/roles/{roleId}/permissions. It carries the complete desired set of permission codes for the target role. Implementation: within a single database transaction, DELETE all rows in erp_hrm_role_permissions WHERE role_id = :roleId, then INSERT one new row per element in permissionCodes (generate a new UUID for each, set role_id = :roleId, permission_code = element value, created_at = now()). Then UPDATE erp_hrm_roles.updated_at = now() for the role. Allowed permission code values: org:manage, employee:manage, employee:view, project:manage, project:view, time:manage, time:approve, time:view_all, report:view. Duplicate codes must be rejected. An empty array is valid and clears all permissions from the role.

IErpHrmRole.ICreate.description:
Request body for creating a new custom role within an organization.

Provide a unique display name for the role and one or more permission codes that define what actions members assigned to this role are allowed to perform. The organization context is supplied via the URL path parameter and must not be repeated in the body.

Built-in roles (Owner, Manager, Employee) are provisioned automatically and cannot be created through this endpoint. The role name must be unique within the organization; a conflict error is returned if the name is already taken.

Available permission codes: `org:manage`, `employee:manage`, `employee:view`, `project:manage`, `project:view`, `time:manage`, `time:approve`, `time:view_all`, `report:view`. Duplicate codes in the request are silently deduplicated.
IErpHrmRole.ICreate.x-autobe-specification: Maps directly to erp_hrm_roles: insert name, is_builtin=false, erp_hrm_organization_id from path. Each string in permissions maps to one row in erp_hrm_role_permissions (role_id, permission_code). Duplicate permission codes are silently deduplicated before insert. Both inserts occur in a single transaction.

IErpHrmOrganization.description: Represents a complete organization record in the ERP HRM platform. An organization is the top-level tenant scope container that isolates all domain data — members, departments, projects, tasks, timelogs, timesheets, employee contracts, and activity logs. Every piece of data in the system belongs to exactly one organization and is invisible to members of other organizations. Each organization carries identity settings (name, description, logo), financial context (currency), temporal context (timezone), and fiscal reporting context (fiscal_start_month). The owner field references the organization member who holds the highest authority within this organization.

All scalar columns (id, name, description, logo_url, currency, timezone, fiscal_start_month, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at) are mapped 1-to-1. The owner_member_id FK column is NOT exposed as a raw scalar; instead the ownerMember relation is resolved via erp_hrm_organization_members (where member_id = owner_member_id AND organization_id = this organization's id) and returned as IErpHrmOrganizationMember.ISummary in the `owner` field. Has-many relations (members, roles, departments, invitations, projects, activityLogs) are excluded from this DTO.

IErpHrmDepartment.ICreate.description:
Request body for creating a new department within an organization.

A department groups organization members by functional area, team, or business unit. Each department must have a name that is unique within its organization. An optional description can provide additional context about the department's purpose.

To create a child department in a two-tier hierarchy, supply a `parentId` referencing an existing top-level department in the same organization. If omitted, the new department is created as a top-level department. Only one level of nesting is supported — a parent department must itself be a top-level department.

The organization context is determined by the `organizationId` path parameter and does not need to be supplied in the request body.
IErpHrmDepartment.ICreate.x-autobe-specification: Maps to erp_hrm_departments table. User-provided fields: name (→ name column, required, unique within organization), description (→ description column, nullable string), parentId (→ parent_id column, nullable UUID). Excluded: id (auto-generated UUID), organization_id (derived from the organizationId path parameter), created_at/updated_at (system-managed timestamps), deleted_at (always NULL on creation), organization (belongs-to relation, not user-provided), parent (belongs-to relation, resolved from parentId), organizationMembers (aggregation, not applicable), children (aggregation, not applicable). Validation: name must be non-empty and unique among non-deleted departments within the same organization. parentId, if provided, must reference an existing non-deleted top-level department (parent_id IS NULL) in the same organization.

Allowed values: 'full-time', 'part-time', 'contractor', 'intern'. Reject with 422 if an invalid value is provided.

IErpHrmInvitation.ICreate.description:
Request body for issuing a new invitation to bring a prospective employee into an organization.

Provide the email address of the person to invite, the role they should be assigned within the organization, and their employment classification. The organization context is established by the path parameter, and the issuing member's identity is resolved automatically from the authenticated session.

If the invited email already belongs to an active platform account, the system will immediately add that person to the organization and mark the invitation as accepted. Otherwise, the invitation will remain pending until the person registers using the invited email address.
IErpHrmInvitation.ICreate.x-autobe-specification: This is the request body DTO for POST /erpHrm/member/organizations/{organizationId}/invitations. It collects the minimum information needed to create an invitation record: the target email address and the onboarding parameters (role and employment type) that are applied if/when the invitee is added as an organization member. The erp_hrm_organization_id is resolved from the path parameter organizationId. The erp_hrm_organization_member_id (issuing member identity) is resolved from the authenticated JWT session. erp_hrm_member_id is server-resolved by looking up erp_hrm_members.email. status defaults to 'pending' (or 'accepted' in the direct-add flow). id, created_at, updated_at are auto-generated. roleId and employmentType are not stored on erp_hrm_invitations but are applied to the erp_hrm_organization_members record created during the direct-add flow.

IErpHrmProject.IRequest.description:
Request body for retrieving a paginated and filtered list of projects within the authenticated member's current organization.

All fields are optional. When omitted, all non-deleted projects in the organization are returned using default pagination settings. The organization scope is automatically determined from the authenticated member's session context — no organization identifier needs to be provided in the request body.

Supports filtering by project lifecycle status and free-text search on project name. Pagination is controlled by page number and items-per-page limit. Results can be sorted by project name, creation date, status, budget hours, or planned dates.
IErpHrmProject.IRequest.x-autobe-specification: This DTO is the request body for the PATCH /erpHrm/member/projects endpoint. It carries optional filter and pagination parameters for querying the erp_hrm_projects table. Implementation steps: (1) Resolve organization_id from the authenticated member's JWT session — it is NOT a field in this DTO. (2) Apply WHERE erp_hrm_projects.organization_id = <session_org_id> AND deleted_at IS NULL. (3) If 'status' is provided (non-null), add AND erp_hrm_projects.status = :status (must be one of: 'active', 'archived', 'completed'; return 400 for unrecognized values). (4) If 'search' is provided, apply AND erp_hrm_projects.name ILIKE '%:search%' leveraging the GIN trigram index on name. (5) Apply ORDER BY <sort> <order>, defaulting to created_at DESC. (6) Apply LIMIT :limit OFFSET (:page - 1) * :limit with defaults: page=1, limit=20. (7) Return IPageIErpHrmProject.ISummary with paginated data and total count metadata.

IErpHrmInvitation.IRequest.description:
Request body for retrieving a paginated and filtered list of invitations within a specific organization.

All fields are optional. When omitted, no filtering is applied for that criterion and default pagination values are used. Multiple status values can be supplied to match invitations in any of those states (e.g., retrieve all pending invitations by passing `["pending"]`).

The `email` field supports partial matching, making it easy to search for invitations sent to a specific domain or address pattern. Date range filters (`createdAtFrom`, `createdAtTo`) allow narrowing results to a specific time window. The `invitingMemberId` filter isolates invitations issued by a particular organization member.
IErpHrmInvitation.IRequest.x-autobe-specification: This is a filter and pagination request DTO for querying erp_hrm_invitations scoped to a specific organization. The organizationId is sourced from the URL path parameter and must not appear here. The authenticated member identity is resolved from the JWT token. Implementation steps: (1) Apply status filter: WHERE erp_hrm_invitations.status IN (...status) if provided, else no status filter. (2) Apply email filter: WHERE erp_hrm_invitations.email ILIKE '%email%' using the GIN trigram index on erp_hrm_invitations.email. (3) Apply invitingMemberId filter: WHERE erp_hrm_invitations.erp_hrm_organization_member_id = invitingMemberId. (4) Apply date range: WHERE erp_hrm_invitations.created_at >= createdAtFrom AND/OR <= createdAtTo. (5) Pagination: offset = (page - 1) * limit, default page=1, default limit=20, max limit=100. (6) Sorting: ORDER BY erp_hrm_invitations.created_at ASC for 'createdAt_asc', DESC for 'createdAt_desc'; default DESC. Use the composite index (erp_hrm_organization_id, status, created_at) for efficient filtering.

status.description: The new status to apply to the invitation. Only `pending` invitations may be updated. Valid target values are: `cancelled` (revoked by an administrator), `rejected` (declined by the invitee or an administrator), or `expired` (explicitly marked as lapsed). Attempting any other transition returns a 422 error.
status.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping to `erp_hrm_invitations.status`. The service layer must enforce: (1) current `status` must be `pending`; (2) new `status` must be one of `cancelled`, `rejected`, or `expired`. The value `accepted` is never valid through this endpoint. On success, persist the new status and update `updated_at` to NOW().

IErpHrmInvitation.IUpdate.description: Request body for updating an existing invitation within an organization. Used exclusively to transition the `status` of a `pending` invitation to one of `cancelled`, `rejected`, or `expired`. All other invitation fields are immutable and managed by the system.
IErpHrmInvitation.IUpdate.x-autobe-specification: Maps exclusively to the `erp_hrm_invitations.status` column. This DTO is the request body for `PUT /erpHrm/member/organizations/{organizationId}/invitations/{invitationId}`. On receipt, the service layer must: (1) verify the authenticated member belongs to the target organization with Owner/Manager permission, (2) fetch the invitation by `id = invitationId` AND `erp_hrm_organization_id = organizationId`, (3) assert the current `status` is `pending` — if not, return 422, (4) assert the requested `status` is one of `cancelled`, `rejected`, or `expired` — if not, return 422, (5) set `status` to the new value and `updated_at` to the current timestamp. The `accepted` transition is never permitted through this endpoint; it is handled internally by the sign-up flow.

Must reference an existing, non-deleted erp_hrm_organization_members record that belongs to the same organization as the target project. The member must have an 'active' status; deactivated members cannot be newly assigned to projects.

'member' grants standard contributor access (time logging, task viewing). 'project-lead' additionally grants task creation, editing, and status management authority within the project.

IErpHrmProjectMember.ICreate.description: Request body for assigning an organization member to a specific project, creating a new project membership record. The target project is identified by the `projectId` path parameter. The caller must provide the UUID of the organization member to assign and the project-scoped role they will hold. Allowed project roles are `member` (a standard contributor who can log time against the project and view its tasks) and `project-lead` (a manager-level role that additionally grants task creation, editing, and status management authority within the project). The target organization member must be active, belong to the same organization as the project, and must not already be assigned to the project.
IErpHrmProjectMember.ICreate.x-autobe-specification: This Create DTO maps directly to an INSERT operation on erp_hrm_project_members. The organization_member_id column is populated from organizationMemberId in the request body. The project_role column is populated from projectRole. The project_id column is derived from the {projectId} path parameter, not from this body. The id is a newly generated UUID. created_at and updated_at are set to the current server timestamp. deleted_at is initialized to null. Validation requirements: (1) organizationMemberId must reference an existing, non-deleted erp_hrm_organization_members record belonging to the same organization as the target project; (2) projectRole must be exactly 'member' or 'project-lead'; (3) a unique constraint check on (organization_member_id, project_id) must pass — if a non-deleted record already exists, return 409 Conflict. The caller must hold the project:manage permission in their organization role.

IErpHrmEmployeeContract.description:
Represents a formal employment contract record for an organization member within the ERP HRM system.

Each contract captures the agreed-upon employment terms at a specific point in time: the monetary compensation amount per pay period (`payRate`), the payment frequency (`payPeriod`), the contracted working hours per week (`workingHoursPerWeek`), the effective start date (`startDate`), an optional end date (`endDate`), and optional supplementary notes.

Contracts are immutable once created. When employment terms change, the active contract is deactivated and a new contract record is created, preserving the full history. The `isActive` flag indicates whether this contract is the currently effective employment agreement for the member. At most one contract per organization member may be active at a time.

Valid values for `payPeriod` are: `hourly`, `daily`, `weekly`, `bi_weekly`, `monthly`, `annually`.
IErpHrmEmployeeContract.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from the erp_hrm_employee_contracts table. All scalar columns are mapped 1:1 to camelCase DTO properties. The FK column organization_member_id is exposed as the scalar UUID field organizationMemberId (not expanded to a nested object), consistent with the operation specification which treats the organizationMemberId as a path parameter and response field. The organizationMember belongs-to relation is excluded from the DTO. pay_period stores one of: 'hourly', 'daily', 'weekly', 'bi_weekly', 'monthly', 'annually'. end_date and notes are nullable (oneOf with null). is_active indicates the currently effective contract; at most one contract per member may be active. Contracts are immutable after creation — updated_at changes only when is_active is toggled.

project_role.description: The new project-scoped role to assign to the membership. Use `member` to grant standard contributor access (time logging, task visibility) or `project-lead` to grant project manager authority (includes creating, editing, and managing tasks within this project). This is the only attribute of a project membership that can be changed after creation.
project_role.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping to erp_hrm_project_members.project_role. Accepted values are exactly 'member' or 'project-lead', enforced by the regex pattern `^(member|project-lead)$`. On PUT, write this value to the project_role column and set updated_at = NOW(). If the submitted value matches the existing value, the update is still processed (no-op result) and the record is returned unchanged.

IErpHrmProjectMember.IUpdate.description: Request body for updating the project-scoped role of an existing project membership. The only mutable attribute of a project membership is the `project_role`, which controls the member's authority level within the project. Supply the desired role value — either `member` for a standard contributor or `project-lead` for a project manager with task management authority. All other membership attributes (the assigned member, parent project, and timestamps) are immutable and are supplied via path parameters or managed by the system.
IErpHrmProjectMember.IUpdate.x-autobe-specification: Maps directly to the erp_hrm_project_members table for the PUT /erpHrm/member/projects/{projectId}/members/{projectMemberId} endpoint. This DTO accepts a single mutable field: project_role. Implementation steps: (1) Validate that project_role is one of the allowed string values: 'member' or 'project-lead'. The pattern constraint `^(member|project-lead)$` enforces this. (2) Perform the UPDATE on erp_hrm_project_members setting project_role = requestBody.project_role and updated_at = NOW() where id = projectMemberId AND project_id = projectId AND deleted_at IS NULL. (3) If the new role is identical to the existing role, proceed with no-op update and return 200 with the current record. Path parameters projectId and projectMemberId are used for record lookup, not present in this DTO. The actor's organization_member_id and created_at are system-managed and excluded.

IErpHrmDepartment.IUpdate.description:
Request body for updating an existing department within an organization.

Allows authorized members (those holding the `org:manage` permission) to modify a department's identifying and structural attributes. The mutable fields are the department's display name, its optional description, and its optional parent department reference that controls placement in the two-tier organizational hierarchy.

The department's name must remain unique within the organization after the update. If a parent department is specified, it must be a top-level department in the same organization (cannot itself have a parent). A department that already has child departments cannot be given a parent, as this would violate the one-level nesting constraint. Setting `parentId` to `null` removes the parent assignment, promoting the department to top-level.

The organization_id and departmentId are resolved from path parameters and not included in the request body. On successful validation, executes: UPDATE erp_hrm_departments SET name=$1, description=$2, parent_id=$3, updated_at=now() WHERE id=departmentId AND organization_id=organizationId AND deleted_at IS NULL. Business validations: (1) name must be unique within organization (@@unique([organization_id, name])), excluding the current department id; (2) parentId if non-null must reference an existing non-deleted department in the same organization with parent_id IS NULL (top-level only); (3) parentId cannot equal departmentId (no self-reference); (4) if the department already has active children (other departments with parent_id = departmentId), parentId cannot be set to non-null, as that would create 2-level nesting depth.

IErpHrmProjectMember.description:
Represents a formal project membership assignment within the ERP HRM system. Each record links an organization member to a specific project, granting them participation rights and defining their project-scoped authority level.

The `projectRole` field determines the member's authority within the project. A `member` role grants standard contributor access — the member can log time against the project and view its tasks. A `project-lead` role additionally grants the authority to create, edit, and manage tasks within the assigned project, without requiring broader organization-level project management permissions.

This record is the prerequisite for time logging against a project and for visibility into project tasks. Each organization member can hold at most one membership per project. Soft-deleted memberships (where `deletedAt` is set) represent historical participation records and are preserved for audit purposes.

The FK column organization_member_id is resolved via JOIN erp_hrm_organization_members (with further joins to erp_hrm_members and user profile data) to produce the nested organizationMember object (IErpHrmOrganizationMember.ISummary). deleted_at is nullable; always included in responses as null or a datetime string. The projectRole value must be one of: 'member' or 'project-lead'.

Valid values for both oldStatus and newStatus are: open, in_progress, completed, and closed. These entries are system-generated upon every task status update and cannot be modified or deleted, ensuring a trustworthy and complete audit trail.
IErpHrmTaskHistory.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_task_histories table. All columns are NOT NULL. The recorder field is resolved by joining erp_hrm_organization_members on erp_hrm_organization_member_id and embedding it as IErpHrmOrganizationMember.ISummary. The taskId field is the raw erp_hrm_task_id FK column exposed for client-side traceability. The task belongs-to relation is not embedded as a full object — taskId is sufficient. Results should default to chronological order (created_at ASC).

IErpHrmTask.description:
Complete detail representation of a task entity within a project in the ERP HRM system.

A task is a discrete unit of work belonging to exactly one project. It carries a title, an optional description, a lifecycle status (open, in-progress, completed, closed), and a priority level (low, medium, high, urgent). Tasks may optionally be assigned to an organization member who is also a project member, and may optionally reference a parent task to form a one-level subtask hierarchy.

This type includes the full chronological audit trail of status transitions (taskHistories), the list of direct subtasks, the summarized parent task reference (when applicable), and the summarized assignee and project context.
IErpHrmTask.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_tasks. Fields: id, title, description (nullable), status, priority, estimated_hours (nullable), due_date (nullable), created_at, updated_at, deleted_at (nullable). JOIN erp_hrm_projects for project summary. JOIN erp_hrm_organization_members for assignee summary (if erp_hrm_organization_member_id is non-null). JOIN erp_hrm_tasks (self) for parent summary (if parent_id is non-null). SELECT subtasks from erp_hrm_tasks WHERE parent_id = taskId AND deleted_at IS NULL. SELECT taskHistories from erp_hrm_task_histories WHERE erp_hrm_task_id = taskId ORDER BY created_at ASC.
