displayName.x-autobe-specification: Maps to the display_name column in the user profile table. Required field — must not be null, empty, or whitespace-only. The minLength:1 constraint enforces a non-empty value at the schema level; the service layer must additionally reject blank/whitespace-only strings with 422 Unprocessable Entity. This value is the human-readable name shown throughout the platform across all organizations the member belongs to.

avatarUrl.description: A URI referencing the member's profile avatar image. Optional — may be set to a new URI to replace the current avatar, or set to `null` to remove the avatar entirely.
avatarUrl.x-autobe-specification: Maps to the avatar_url column in the user profile table. Optional and nullable. Pass a valid URI string to set or replace the avatar image; pass null to explicitly clear (remove) the current avatar. The URI format is validated at the schema level (format: uri). No format transformation is required — store the URI value as-is.

phoneNumber.description: A contact phone number for the member. Optional — may be set, changed, or cleared (by passing `null`) at any time. Any string format is accepted.
phoneNumber.x-autobe-specification: Maps to the phone_number column in the user profile table. Optional and nullable. Store the value as-is.

IErpHrmGuestSession.IUpdate.description: Request body for updating the authenticated member's global user profile. The profile is a platform-wide identity shared across all organizations the member belongs to — any accepted change is immediately reflected everywhere without additional synchronization. The `displayName` field is required and must not be empty or blank. The `avatarUrl` and `phoneNumber` fields are optional; passing `null` for either explicitly clears the current value.
IErpHrmGuestSession.IUpdate.x-autobe-specification: This DTO is the request body for the user profile update operation at PUT /erpHrm/member/profile. It maps to the UserProfile entity stored in a platform-level user profile table (joined with erp_hrm_members via member_id). The authenticated member identity is resolved from the JWT token — it must never be accepted from the request body. Implementation: (1) Extract member id from JWT. (2) Load current UserProfile record. (3) Validate displayName is non-empty/non-blank. (4) Perform no-op detection — if all incoming values equal stored values, return current profile without DB write or event emission. Fields: displayName → display_name column; avatarUrl → avatar_url column (nullable); phoneNumber → phone_number column (nullable).

IErpHrmTask.ISummary.description:
Lightweight summary representation of a task within a project, used in paginated list responses.

Each task record captures the essential attributes needed for list display: its unique identifier, title, current status, priority level, optional estimated effort in hours, and optional due date. The optional assignee is returned as a condensed organization member summary.

The `parentId` field serves as a subtask indicator — when non-null, this task is a subtask of the referenced parent task. Only one level of nesting is permitted in the system.

This summary type excludes large descriptive text and nested child collections (subtasks, task histories, timelogs) to keep list responses compact and performant.
IErpHrmTask.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from the erp_hrm_tasks table. Scalar columns mapped directly: id, title, status, priority, estimated_hours (as estimatedHours, nullable Float → number | null), due_date (as dueDate, nullable Timestamptz → string date-time | null), parent_id (as parentId, nullable UUID → string uuid | null — scalar subtask indicator only), created_at, updated_at, deleted_at (nullable). Relation: assignee resolved via LEFT JOIN erp_hrm_organization_members on erp_hrm_organization_member_id, returned as IErpHrmOrganizationMember.ISummary or null. The project relation and erp_hrm_project_id column are omitted as the project context is established via the API path parameter. The description column, parent relation object, and all has-many relations (subtasks, taskHistories, timelogs, timers) are excluded to keep the summary payload compact and performant for paginated list views.

IErpHrmInvitation.ISummary.description: A lightweight summary record representing a single invitation within an organization, used in paginated list responses. Each invitation captures the intent to onboard a specific individual (identified by their email address) into the organization. The `status` field reflects the current lifecycle stage of the invitation: `pending` (awaiting the invitee's registration), `accepted` (the invitee has registered and been linked), `rejected`, `expired`, or `cancelled`. The `invitingMember` property identifies the organization member who issued the invitation. IErpHrmEmployeeContract.IRequest.description:
Search criteria, filters, and pagination parameters for retrieving the employment contract history of a specific organization member.

All fields are optional. When omitted, no filtering is applied for that dimension and results include all contracts for the target member. The default ordering is chronological (ascending by start date), and the default page size is 20 records per page.

The `startDate` and `endDate` range objects allow filtering contracts by their effective date boundaries. The `isActive` flag can narrow results to only the current active contract or only historical contracts. Use `includeOpenEnded` to also include contracts with no predetermined end date.

The organizationMemberId path parameter and the authenticated member's session identity are resolved externally — they must NOT appear in this body. Query erp_hrm_employee_contracts WHERE organization_member_id = :organizationMemberId. Apply each optional filter when present: isActive maps to is_active boolean column; payPeriod maps to pay_period string column; startDate maps to start_date column range (gte/lte); endDate maps to end_date column range (gte/lte, excluding null rows); includeOpenEnded=true also includes rows where end_date IS NULL. Request body for creating a new draft timesheet for the currently authenticated organization member.

A timesheet covers exactly one calendar week, identified by its start date (always a Monday) and end date (always the following Sunday). The authenticated member's identity is derived from the session and does not need to be supplied. Upon successful creation, the timesheet is placed in 'draft' status.

No two timesheets for the same member may cover the same week; submitting a duplicate week will result in a conflict error.

All other fields (id, reviewer_id, submitted_at, reviewed_at, rejection_reason, created_at, updated_at) are server-managed and must not be accepted from the request body. IErpHrmTimelog.IRequest.description:
Request body for the paginated timelog list endpoint (`PATCH /erpHrm/member/timelogs`). All fields are optional and combinable. Supports filtering by date range, project, task, billable status, and organization member. Pagination is controlled via `page` and `limit`.

All fields are optional and combinable. Implementation steps:
1. Resolve the authenticated member's organization context from the JWT session.
2. Determine access scope: if the caller does NOT have the 'time:view_all' permission, force organization_member_id = caller's own organization_member_id regardless of memberOrganizationMemberId.
3. Apply optional WHERE filters: work_date >= startDate, work_date <= endDate, project_id = projectId, task_id = taskId, billable = billable, organization_member_id = memberOrganizationMemberId (only if privileged).
4. Validate projectId exists in organization (404 if not). Validate taskId belongs to projectId if both provided (400 if not).
5. Pagination: OFFSET = (page - 1) * limit; default limit = 20. Sort: work_date DESC, created_at DESC.

IErpHrmTaskHistory.description:
A single immutable task history entry representing one status transition event on a task within the ERP HRM system.

Each TaskHistory record is automatically created by the system whenever a task's status changes. It captures the status before the transition (`oldStatus`), the status after the transition (`newStatus`), the exact timestamp of the change (`createdAt`), and the organization member who performed the change (`recorder`).

Valid values for `oldStatus` and `newStatus` are: `open`, `in_progress`, `completed`, and `closed`. These entries form a chronological, append-only audit trail for the full lifecycle of any given task.

TaskHistory records are strictly read-only — they cannot be created, modified, or deleted through the API.

The `organizationMember` relation (FK: erp_hrm_organization_member_id → erp_hrm_organization_members.id) is joined and returned as IErpHrmOrganizationMember.ISummary under the DTO key `recorder`. Both FK scalar columns (erp_hrm_task_id and erp_hrm_organization_member_id) are excluded from the DTO since they are exposed as rich objects. This table has no updated_at or deleted_at — records are strictly immutable and append-only.

Any other transition returns 422.

IErpHrmTimelog.ISummary.description:
Lightweight summary representation of a timelog record, used in paginated list responses.

Each timelog captures a discrete work session performed by an organization member on a specific date, tied to a project and optionally a task. The `durationMinutes` field stores the session length in whole minutes. The `billable` flag indicates whether the work counts against a project budget or client billing.

The `timesheetId` field is critical for rendering list views: when non-null and the referenced timesheet is in `submitted` or `approved` status, the timelog is a protected record and must be treated as read-only by the client.

The `organizationMember`, `project`, and `task` fields are pre-expanded summary objects for convenient display without additional lookups.

Scalar columns id, work_date, duration_minutes, billable, description, created_at, updated_at are projected directly. The FK columns organization_member_id, project_id, task_id are excluded because their corresponding belongs-to relations (organizationMember, project, task) are JOIN-expanded into ISummary objects. timesheet_id is surfaced as a raw UUID scalar (timesheetId) rather than a nested object so clients can detect locked records without an extra join to load full timesheet state. The timesheet belongs-to relation is excluded; only the scalar ID is included. Sort order is work_date DESC, created_at DESC as specified.

IErpHrmTimer.IRequest.description: Request body for searching and paginating active timer sessions via PATCH /erpHrm/member/timers. All filter fields are optional. A member without the `time:view_all` permission will always have results restricted to their own active timer regardless of filters. A member with `time:view_all` may use `organizationMemberId` to narrow results to a specific member. Supports filtering by project, member assignment, and whether a task is linked. Pagination and sort direction are configurable.
IErpHrmTimer.IRequest.x-autobe-specification: Filter and pagination DTO for PATCH /erpHrm/member/timers. Queries erp_hrm_timers joined with erp_hrm_organization_members (for organization scoping), erp_hrm_projects, and optionally erp_hrm_tasks. Authorization: members without time:view_all permission are always restricted to their own timer (organization_member_id = current member id); members with time:view_all may browse all organization timers and may use organizationMemberId to narrow to a specific member. Filters: projectId -> WHERE project_id = :projectId on erp_hrm_timers; organizationMemberId -> WHERE organization_member_id = :organizationMemberId (only when requester has time:view_all); hasTask -> true: WHERE task_id IS NOT NULL, false: WHERE task_id IS NULL, omitted/null: no filter. Sorting: sortBy='started_at' with sortOrder='asc'|'desc', default started_at DESC. Pagination: page (1-based integer, default 1) and limit (integer 1-100, default 20). Always scope to requester's current organization context.

rejection_reason.description: Mandatory written explanation provided by the reviewer when declining a timesheet. Must be a non-empty string. This reason is stored on the timesheet record and displayed to the employee so they understand what needs to be corrected before they can resubmit.
rejection_reason.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping to erp_hrm_timesheets.rejection_reason (nullable String?). Although the DB column allows null, the rejection action requires a non-empty value — validate that the trimmed value is non-null and non-empty; return 422 if blank or null. Persisted via UPDATE erp_hrm_timesheets SET rejection_reason = (this value) WHERE id = {timesheetId}.

IErpHrmTimesheet.IReject.description: Request body for rejecting a submitted timesheet on behalf of an authorized reviewer. Contains only the mandatory written reason explaining why the timesheet is being declined. The reviewer's identity is resolved automatically from the authenticated session. Used exclusively by members holding the `time:approve` permission.
IErpHrmTimesheet.IReject.x-autobe-specification: This is the request body for the reject timesheet action (POST /erpHrm/member/timesheets/{timesheetId}/reject). It carries only the mandatory rejection_reason string. Implementation: validate that rejection_reason is non-null and non-empty after trimming whitespace (return 422 if blank or null). Then execute: UPDATE erp_hrm_timesheets SET status='rejected', rejection_reason=(this.rejection_reason), reviewer_id=(JWT member's organization_member_id), reviewed_at=NOW(), updated_at=NOW() WHERE id={timesheetId} AND status='submitted'. The acting reviewer's identity is resolved entirely from the authenticated member session JWT — no reviewer fields are present in this DTO.

IErpHrmInvitation.description:
Full detail representation of an invitation record in the ERP HRM system.

An invitation captures the organizational intent to onboard a prospective employee. It is directed at a specific email address and scoped to a single organization. The invitation lifecycle progresses through the following statuses: `pending` (issued and awaiting registration), `accepted` (the invitee has registered and been linked to the organization), `rejected` (declined), `expired` (validity period exceeded), or `cancelled` (revoked by an administrator or the issuing member).

The `memberId` field is `null` while the invitation is in the `pending` state and is populated with the platform-level member account ID once the invitee has registered or been matched. The `organization` and `invitingMember` fields provide embedded summary context about the organizational scope and who issued the invitation respectively.
IErpHrmInvitation.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_invitations table. Scalar columns id, email, status, created_at, updated_at are mapped directly. The FK column erp_hrm_organization_id is resolved via JOIN to erp_hrm_organizations and returned as IErpHrmOrganization.ISummary in the 'organization' field. The FK column erp_hrm_organization_member_id is resolved via JOIN to erp_hrm_organization_members and returned as IErpHrmOrganizationMember.ISummary in the 'invitingMember' field. The FK column erp_hrm_member_id is returned as the raw UUID in 'memberId' (nullable: null when invitation is pending, populated on acceptance). The 'member' belongs-to relation is not expanded as a nested object; only the raw UUID is exposed.

details.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_activity_logs.details (nullable String?). Optional supplementary context for the action. For example, a role change may include old and new role names; a timesheet rejection may include the rejection reason. Null when no additional context is needed.

created_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_activity_logs.created_at (DateTime @db.Timestamptz). Recorded by the system at the exact moment the business event is processed. This is the only timestamp column on this table; entries are immutable and have no updated_at or deleted_at.

IErpHrmActivityLog.ISummary.description:
Lightweight summary representation of an organizational activity log entry, used in paginated list responses.

Each entry is an immutable, system-generated audit record capturing a significant business event that occurred within the organization. The entry identifies the kind of action that took place (action_type), the type and identity of the business entity that was affected (target_entity_type and target_entity_id), the organization member who performed the action (performer), and any supplementary contextual details.

Activity log entries are permanently preserved and cannot be created, modified, or deleted through any user-facing operation. The created_at timestamp records the exact moment the event was processed by the system.
IErpHrmActivityLog.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_activity_logs. All scalar columns (id, action_type, target_entity_type, target_entity_id, organization_member_id, details, created_at) are included directly. The performer belongs-to relation is resolved via JOIN on erp_hrm_organization_members where organization_member_id = erp_hrm_organization_members.id, and returned as IErpHrmOrganizationMember.ISummary. organization_id is excluded because the organization context is determined by the authenticated member session. The organization belongs-to relation is also excluded for the same reason. No updated_at or deleted_at columns exist on this table — entries are immutable and append-only.

targetMemberId.description: The unique identifier (`erp_hrm_organization_members.id`) of the organization member who will receive the Owner role. The designated member must already be an active member of this organization and must not currently hold the Owner role.
targetMemberId.x-autobe-specification: Cross-table FK referencing erp_hrm_organization_members.id — the per-organization identity record of the member who will receive the Owner role. Not a direct column of erp_hrm_organizations. The service must: (a) look up the erp_hrm_organization_members record by this id and verify it belongs to the organizationId from the path, (b) verify status = 'active', (c) verify the member does not already hold the built-in Owner role. After validation, set this member's erp_hrm_organization_members.role_id to the Owner role ID and update erp_hrm_organizations.owner_member_id to this member's erp_hrm_members.id.

outgoingOwnerRoleId.description: The unique identifier (`erp_hrm_roles.id`) of the non-Owner role within this organization that the outgoing owner will be reassigned to after the transfer. Must be a valid role belonging to this organization and must not be the built-in Owner role.
outgoingOwnerRoleId.x-autobe-specification: Cross-table FK referencing erp_hrm_roles.id — the role within this organization that the outgoing owner (the caller) will be reassigned to after the transfer completes. Not a direct column of erp_hrm_organizations. The service must: (a) look up the erp_hrm_roles record by this id, (b) verify erp_hrm_roles.erp_hrm_organization_id = the organizationId from the path, (c) verify it is NOT the built-in Owner role (is_builtin = true AND name = 'Owner'). After validation, set the caller's erp_hrm_organization_members.role_id to this value in the transaction.

IErpHrmOrganization.ITransferOwnership.description:
Request body for transferring organization ownership from the current Owner to another active member.

The caller must be the current Owner of the organization (identified by the `organizationId` path parameter). They specify which existing active organization member should receive the Owner role (`targetMemberId`), and which non-Owner role they themselves should be demoted to after the transfer (`outgoingOwnerRoleId`).

Both fields are required. The target member must be an active member of the organization and must not already hold the Owner role. The outgoing owner role must be a valid role within the organization that is not the built-in Owner role.
IErpHrmOrganization.ITransferOwnership.x-autobe-specification:
This is the request body DTO for POST /erpHrm/member/organizations/{organizationId}/ownership/transfer. It carries two FK references needed to execute the ownership transfer transaction atomically:
1. targetMemberId: the erp_hrm_organization_members.id of the member who will receive the Owner role. The service layer must verify: (a) this member belongs to the organization identified by the path parameter organizationId, (b) has status='active', (c) is not already the Owner.
2. outgoingOwnerRoleId: the erp_hrm_roles.id that the current owner (caller) will be reassigned to after the transfer. The service layer must verify: (a) this role belongs to the same organization, (b) is NOT the built-in Owner role.
Transaction steps: (a) set target member's erp_hrm_organization_members.role_id to the Owner role ID, (b) set caller's erp_hrm_organization_members.role_id to outgoingOwnerRoleId, (c) update erp_hrm_organizations.owner_member_id to the target member's erp_hrm_members.id (platform-level member FK), (d) set updated_at=NOW() on both erp_hrm_organization_members records and the erp_hrm_organizations record. Returns the updated IErpHrmOrganization.

IErpHrmTimesheet.ISummary.description:
Lightweight summary representation of a timesheet record, returned as items in paginated list responses.

A timesheet groups an employee's work sessions (timelogs) for a single calendar week (Monday through Sunday) and tracks the submission and approval lifecycle. The status field reflects the current state: 'draft' (not yet submitted), 'submitted' (awaiting review), 'approved' (accepted by reviewer), or 'rejected' (declined, returned to draft for revision).

The total_hours figure is computed from the sum of all associated timelog durations and is not stored directly on the timesheet record. For timesheets that have been reviewed (approved or rejected), the reviewer's identity, reviewed_at timestamp, and (if rejected) rejection_reason are included to provide a clear audit trail.
IErpHrmTimesheet.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: Fetch the timesheet row from erp_hrm_timesheets by id. Join erp_hrm_organization_members on organization_member_id to populate the owner field as IErpHrmOrganizationMember.ISummary. Left-join erp_hrm_organization_members on reviewer_id to populate the reviewer field as IErpHrmOrganizationMember.ISummary (null when reviewer_id IS NULL). Compute total_hours by summing the duration values of all erp_hrm_timelogs rows WHERE timesheet_id = this timesheet's id; return 0.0 when no timelogs exist. Expose scalar columns directly: id (UUID), status (string enum: draft/submitted/approved/rejected), week_start_date (Monday, date-time), week_end_date (Sunday, date-time), submitted_at (nullable date-time), reviewed_at (nullable date-time), rejection_reason (nullable string), created_at, updated_at. Exclude raw FK columns organization_member_id and reviewer_id from the response.

Clients use this value together with the current wall-clock time to compute elapsed duration in real time. The server does NOT compute or return elapsed seconds.

created_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_timers.created_at (DateTime @db.Timestamptz). Set to now() on insert, effectively equal to started_at. Retained for audit consistency with other entities in the system.

IErpHrmTimer.description:
A full detail representation of an active real-time tracking timer session owned by an organization member.

A timer is a transient record that captures a live work session in progress. Each member may have at most one active timer at any given time. The timer is bound to exactly one project and optionally to one task within that project. The `started_at` timestamp marks the exact moment the session began, allowing clients to compute elapsed duration in real time.

Timer records do not have `updated_at` or `deleted_at` fields — they are permanently removed from the database when the member stops the timer (which produces a Timelog) or discards it (no Timelog created). This type is returned by timer creation, retrieval, and update operations.
IErpHrmTimer.x-autobe-specification: This DTO maps directly to the erp_hrm_timers table. Scalar fields (id, description, started_at, created_at) are direct column mappings. The three FK columns (organization_member_id, project_id, task_id) are NOT exposed as raw IDs; instead they are resolved via JOIN and returned as nested ISummary objects: organizationMember (JOIN erp_hrm_organization_members), project (JOIN erp_hrm_projects), task (LEFT JOIN erp_hrm_tasks — nullable when task_id IS NULL). No updated_at or deleted_at columns exist on erp_hrm_timers — the record is permanently deleted upon stop or discard. Elapsed duration is NOT computed server-side; clients derive it from started_at.

statuses.description: Optional list of timesheet statuses to filter by. When provided, only timesheets whose current status matches one of the specified values are returned. Allowed values: 'draft', 'submitted', 'approved', 'rejected'. When omitted, timesheets of all statuses are included subject to the caller's permission level.
statuses.x-autobe-specification: Filter parameter mapping to erp_hrm_timesheets.status column. Applied as: WHERE status IN (...statuses). Allowed values: 'draft', 'submitted', 'approved', 'rejected'. When omitted or empty, no status restriction is applied and timesheets of all statuses are returned (subject to the caller's access level). Multiple values may be combined.

startDate.description: Optional inclusive lower bound for the timesheet week start date filter. When provided, only timesheets whose calendar week begins on or after this date are returned. Should be an ISO 8601 date-time value, ideally aligned to a Monday. When omitted, no lower date boundary is applied.
startDate.x-autobe-specification: Filter parameter mapping to erp_hrm_timesheets.week_start_date column. Applied as: WHERE week_start_date >= startDate. ISO 8601 date-time value representing the inclusive lower bound of the calendar week start date range. When omitted, no lower bound is applied on week_start_date.

endDate.description: Optional inclusive upper bound for the timesheet week end date filter. When provided, only timesheets whose calendar week ends on or before this date are returned. Should be an ISO 8601 date-time value, ideally aligned to a Sunday. When omitted, no upper date boundary is applied.
endDate.x-autobe-specification: Filter parameter mapping to erp_hrm_timesheets.week_end_date column. Applied as: WHERE week_end_date <= endDate. ISO 8601 date-time value representing the inclusive upper bound of the calendar week end date range. When omitted, no upper bound is applied on week_end_date.

organizationMemberId.description: Optional UUID of a specific organization member whose timesheets to retrieve. Only honored for callers with 'time_approve' or 'time_view_all' permission. When provided by a privileged caller, only timesheets owned by that member are returned. Regular members without elevated permissions are always scoped to their own timesheets regardless of this field. When omitted by a privileged caller, timesheets from all accessible members are returned.
organizationMemberId.x-autobe-specification: Filter parameter mapping to erp_hrm_timesheets.organization_member_id column. Applied as: WHERE organization_member_id = organizationMemberId. This filter is ONLY honored when the authenticated caller holds 'time_approve' or 'time_view_all' permission. If the caller lacks these permissions, this field is silently ignored and the query is automatically scoped to the caller's own organization_member_id. When omitted by a privileged caller, all organization members' timesheets are included within their permission scope.

page.description: Optional 1-based page number for paginated results. Determines which page of the result set to return. Defaults to 1 (the first page) when omitted. Must be a positive integer of at least 1.
page.x-autobe-specification: Pagination query parameter with no direct DB column. Used to compute SQL OFFSET: OFFSET = (page - 1) * limit. 1-based page number; default is 1 when omitted. Minimum value is 1. Combined with the limit parameter to produce bounded, paginated result sets.

limit.description: Optional maximum number of timesheet records to return per page. Controls the page size of the paginated result. Defaults to 20 when omitted. Must be between 1 and 100 inclusive.
limit.x-autobe-specification: Pagination query parameter with no direct DB column. Applied as the SQL LIMIT clause. Controls how many timesheet records are returned per page. Default is 20 when omitted. Minimum is 1, maximum is 100. Combined with the page parameter to produce bounded, paginated result sets.

IErpHrmTimesheet.IRequest.description: Request body for the timesheet list endpoint, providing optional filters and pagination parameters. Allows authenticated members to query their own timesheets, while members with elevated permissions (time_approve or time_view_all) can additionally filter by a specific organization member's timesheets or browse all timesheets across the organization. All fields are optional. When no filters are provided, the results are scoped by the caller's access level and returned in reverse chronological order by week start date.
IErpHrmTimesheet.IRequest.x-autobe-specification: This request DTO provides optional filter and pagination parameters for querying the erp_hrm_timesheets table. It does not map to a single database table — it is a composite query parameter object. Source tables: erp_hrm_timesheets (primary), erp_hrm_organization_members (join to scope by organization_id). Filter mappings: statuses → WHERE status IN (...statuses) on erp_hrm_timesheets.status; startDate → WHERE week_start_date >= startDate; endDate → WHERE week_end_date <= endDate; organizationMemberId → WHERE organization_member_id = organizationMemberId (only honored if caller has time_approve or time_view_all permission; otherwise ignored and caller's own organization_member_id is used). Pagination: page is 1-based page number (default: 1), limit is page size (default: 20, max: 100). Sorting default: ORDER BY week_start_date DESC. All filters are optional; omitting a filter means no restriction on that dimension.

Used to derive the computed `locked` field: locked = (timesheet != null && timesheet.status == 'approved').

duration_minutes.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_timelogs.duration_minutes (Integer). Must be a positive integer (>= 1). Stored in whole minutes to avoid floating-point precision issues when summing across multiple timelogs.

billable.description: Indicates whether this work session is billable to a client or counts against a project budget. `true` means the time is billable; `false` means it is non-billable (e.g., internal work).
billable.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_timelogs.billable (Boolean). Defaults to false when not explicitly provided at creation. For timelogs created from a stopped timer, defaults to true.

description.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_timelogs.description (String?). Nullable. Supports full-text search in list queries. Null when no description was provided.

Specifically: if timesheet_id is null → locked = false; if timesheet_id is non-null and timesheet.status == 'approved' → locked = true; otherwise → locked = false. created_at.description: The UTC timestamp when this timelog record was first created.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_timelogs.created_at (Timestamptz). Set to the current UTC timestamp at the time the timelog record is first inserted. Never modified after creation.

updated_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_timelogs.updated_at (Timestamptz). Set to the current UTC timestamp at creation and updated to the current UTC timestamp whenever any field on the timelog record is modified.

IErpHrmTimelog.description:
Complete detail record of a timelog entry representing a discrete completed work session owned by an organization member.

A timelog captures the date on which work was performed, the duration of the session in whole minutes, whether the session is billable, the project under which the work was done, and optionally the specific task the work relates to. It may also be linked to a weekly timesheet once the member submits their work hours for review.

The `locked` field indicates whether the timelog is currently immutable due to its linked timesheet having been approved. When `locked` is `true`, update and delete operations on this timelog will be rejected. The lock is lifted if the timesheet is subsequently rejected and returned to draft status.

The `owner` field provides the identity of the organization member who created and owns this timelog. The `project` and `task` fields provide lightweight summaries of the associated work context. The `timesheet` field is present when the timelog has been included in a weekly timesheet submission.
IErpHrmTimelog.x-autobe-specification: Fetch a single erp_hrm_timelogs record by id. JOIN erp_hrm_organization_members (via organization_member_id) and return as IErpHrmOrganizationMember.ISummary for the owner field. JOIN erp_hrm_projects (via project_id) and return as IErpHrmProject.ISummary for the project field. LEFT JOIN erp_hrm_tasks (via task_id) and return as IErpHrmTask.ISummary or null for the task field. LEFT JOIN erp_hrm_timesheets (via timesheet_id) and return as IErpHrmTimesheet.ISummary or null for the timesheet field. Compute locked = (timesheet != null && timesheet.status == 'approved'). All scalar columns (id, work_date, duration_minutes, billable, description, created_at, updated_at) are direct mappings from erp_hrm_timelogs.

IErpHrmTimesheet.description:
Full detail representation of a weekly timesheet record owned by an organization member.

A timesheet covers exactly one calendar week, defined by its `weekStartDate` (always a Monday) and `weekEndDate` (always the following Sunday). Timesheets progress through a review lifecycle: draft → submitted → approved or rejected. A rejected timesheet returns to draft status, allowing the employee to revise their timelogs and resubmit.

The `totalMinutes` field is computed from the sum of all associated timelog durations and is not stored directly in the database. The `reviewer` field is populated once a manager has acted on the timesheet (approved or rejected), along with the `reviewedAt` timestamp. If the timesheet was rejected, `rejectionReason` contains the mandatory explanation provided by the reviewer.
IErpHrmTimesheet.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_timesheets. owner: JOIN erp_hrm_organization_members ON organization_member_id = id → IErpHrmOrganizationMember.ISummary. reviewer: LEFT JOIN erp_hrm_organization_members ON reviewer_id = id → nullable IErpHrmOrganizationMember.ISummary. timelogs: SELECT * FROM erp_hrm_timelogs WHERE timesheet_id = this.id → IErpHrmTimelog.ISummary[]. total_minutes: SUM(duration_minutes) FROM erp_hrm_timelogs WHERE timesheet_id = this.id; defaults to 0 when no timelogs exist.

IErpHrmActivityLog.description: Full detail representation of a single immutable organizational audit trail entry. Each entry is written automatically by the system whenever a qualifying business event occurs within an organization (such as employee lifecycle events, contract operations, project changes, task status updates, timesheet lifecycle events, or role assignments). Once created, an entry is permanent and can never be edited or deleted. The `action_type` identifies the category of event from a fixed set of recognized values. The `performer` provides the organization member who carried out the action. The `target_entity_type` and `target_entity_id` together identify the specific business object that was affected.
IErpHrmActivityLog.x-autobe-specification: Direct read mapping from erp_hrm_activity_logs. All scalar columns (id, organization_id, action_type, target_entity_type, target_entity_id, details, created_at) are returned as-is. The organization_member_id FK column is resolved via JOIN to erp_hrm_organization_members (and transitively to erp_hrm_members for platform-level identity) to produce the 'performer' property as IErpHrmOrganizationMember.ISummary. The 'organization' belongs-to relation is not expanded in the response — organization context is conveyed via organization_id. This is a pure read DTO; no write operations are performed. Entries are immutable: no updated_at or deleted_at columns exist on this table.

IErpHrmActivityLog.IRequest.description:
Request body for searching and paginating activity log entries within the authenticated member's current organization.

All fields are optional. When omitted, all activity log entries for the organization are returned in descending chronological order. The organization scope is automatically determined from the authenticated member's JWT session and cannot be overridden by this request body.

Supports multi-value filtering on action_type and target_entity_type, UUID-based filtering for a specific target entity or performer, and date-time range filtering on the created_at timestamp. Pagination and sort controls are also available.
IErpHrmActivityLog.IRequest.x-autobe-specification:
This is a read-only query filter DTO — no database writes occur. Implementation steps:
1. organization_id is NOT accepted from the client; it is always resolved from the authenticated member's current JWT session context.
2. action_type: optional array of action type strings; if provided, apply WHERE action_type IN (...) against erp_hrm_activity_logs. Valid values: 'employee_invited', 'employee_deactivated', 'employee_reactivated', 'contract_created', 'contract_edited', 'project_created', 'project_archived', 'project_completed', 'project_deleted', 'task_status_changed', 'timesheet_submitted', 'timesheet_approved', 'timesheet_rejected', 'role_assigned_or_changed'.
3. target_entity_type: optional array of entity type strings; if provided, apply WHERE target_entity_type IN (...). Valid values: 'member', 'contract', 'project', 'task', 'timesheet', 'role'.
4. target_entity_id: optional UUID; if provided, apply WHERE target_entity_id = $value.
5. organization_member_id: optional UUID; if provided, apply WHERE organization_member_id = $value.
6. created_at_from: optional ISO 8601 datetime; if provided, apply WHERE created_at >= $value (inclusive).
7. created_at_to: optional ISO 8601 datetime; if provided, apply WHERE created_at <= $value (inclusive).
8. pagination: optional nested object with page and limit sub-fields. If both this nested object and top-level page/limit fields are provided, top-level fields take precedence.
9. sort: optional nested object with field ('created_at' or 'action_type') and direction ('asc' or 'desc'). Default: created_at DESC.
10. page: top-level 1-based page number for offset calculation (offset = (page - 1) * limit). Default: 1.
11. limit: top-level maximum records per page. Default: 20. Max: 100.
12. Leverage @@index([organization_id, created_at]) and @@index([organization_id, action_type]) on erp_hrm_activity_logs for efficient filtering.
13. If a filter references a non-existent member_id or entity_id, return empty results (not an error).

IErpHrmMember.ISummary.description: Lightweight summary representation of a platform-level member account, used wherever a member identity reference is needed in API responses. Provides the essential identifying fields — unique identifier, email address, and registration timestamp — without exposing sensitive credentials or heavy lifecycle data. This summary type appears as the `member` property on session records and organization member entries, and as the `owner` property on organizations. It is sufficient for display purposes, user lookups, and audit trail attribution.

Select id (primary key UUID), email (unique login identifier), and created_at (account registration timestamp). Exclude password_hash for security. Exclude updated_at and deleted_at as they are not needed in summary display contexts. Exclude all relations (sessions, passwordResets, ownedOrganizations, organizationMembers, invitations) as they are not part of this summary. All three included fields are NOT NULL in the database, so all are required.

When null or omitted, no lower bound restriction is applied.

IErpHrmMember.description: Represents a registered member's public platform-level identity on the ERP HRM platform. Each member is uniquely identified by their UUID and email address, which serves as the global login identifier across all organizations. Sensitive credentials such as the password hash are never exposed in API responses. The `deleted_at` field signals whether the account is active (null) or has been deactivated (non-null timestamp).
IErpHrmMember.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_members table. Query the erp_hrm_members row by id and return: id, email, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at. Never include password_hash in any response. Relation collections (sessions, passwordResets, ownedOrganizations, organizationMembers, invitations) are excluded — access them via their own dedicated endpoints. The deleted_at field is always returned: null when the account is active, an ISO 8601 timestamp when the account has been soft-deleted.
